points.name: FiiO
points.description: Chinese audio manufacturer producing portable music players, headphone amplifiers, and in-ear monitors for enthusiast listeners.
points.bullets:
An audio equipment manufacturer that designs and builds finished personal-audio hardware, including portable digital audio players, desktop headphone amplifiers, DACs, in-ear monitors, headphones and streamers for the consumer audiophile market.
1. An audio equipment maker that builds digital audio players, headphone amplifiers and DACs sold as finished hardware running standalone for consumers.
2. The products integrate discrete DAC chips, R-2R ladder DACs, planar magnetic drivers, THX amplification circuits and Bluetooth codecs in portable and desktop chassis.
3. The products deliver high-resolution digital-to-analog conversion, headphone amplification, spatial audio reproduction and wireless high-resolution audio streaming.
4. Customers receive finished hardware devices, including digital audio players, headphone amplifiers, DACs, headphones and in-ear monitors.
5. The devices are used in personal listening setups, desktop hi-fi systems and portable audiophile applications.
6. The company sells to consumers and audiophile enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through consumer electronics retail channels.
8. The company distinguishes itself by packing desktop-grade audiophile components into portable form factors and releasing feature-rich products at competitive prices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses components from AKM, ESS Technology, Qualcomm and Sony, and operates the Snowsky and JadeAudio sub-brands.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company and a parent brand to multiple subsidiary audio brands.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established manufacturer with a broad product lineup and a rapid release cadence.
Geography: It is based in China and operates in the global market with a focus on North America.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Splice
points.description: New York music technology company providing a royalty-free sample library and rent-to-own software for creators.
points.bullets:
A music creation platform and sample marketplace that provides a royalty-free sample library, AI-driven sound suggestion and generation tools, and rent-to-own software plugins for musicians and producers.
1. A music technology company and software marketplace that builds AI tools and sample libraries sold as a subscription platform running inside digital audio workstations.
2. A cloud-based sample library accessed via a desktop plugin, combined with generative audio algorithms and voice cloning models.
3. Sample search and recommendation, stem processing, generative audio variation creation, and voice cloning.
4. Software products, desktop plugins, subscription services, and rent-to-own VST synthesizers.
5. Digital audio workstations, music production studios, and sound design workflows.
6. Musicians, producers, sound designers, and creators.
7. Its platform and plugins are used directly by creators and integrated into digital audio workstations by software developers.
8. It combines a royalty-free sample marketplace with rent-to-own software plugins and acquired generative AI voice cloning technologies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its platform is integrated into Pro Tools and Fender Studio Pro, and it has acquired Spitfire Audio and Kits AI.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Subscription fees for sample libraries and AI tools, plus rent-to-own payment plans for software.
Scale and maturity: A company that completed seed funding and has restructured its debt while acquiring other music technology firms.
Geography: Based in New York, US.
Beyond audio: It is focused entirely on music creation, sound design, and audio production tools.

points.name: KEF
points.description: British audio brand making high-fidelity speakers for home listening.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and consumer audio equipment that designs and manufactures high-fidelity loudspeakers, active wireless speakers, subwoofers, soundbars and earphones for audiophile consumers and home audio installers.
1. A maker of finished audio hardware that builds active and passive loudspeakers sold as physical products running integrated amplification, digital signal processing and wireless streaming platforms.
2. The core technologies are proprietary acoustic transducer designs, including coaxial Uni-Q driver arrays and Uni-Core low-frequency driver arrays, combined with Metamaterial Absorption Technology for high-frequency absorption and integrated Class D and Class A/B amplification.
3. The audio capabilities delivered are high-fidelity music reproduction, spatial audio decoding for Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, wireless multiroom streaming, low-frequency bass extension and acoustic cabinet vibration cancellation.
4. The organization provides finished hardware products, companion control and streaming software applications and optional physical accessories.
5. The devices are used in home stereo systems, home cinema setups, desktop listening environments and portable personal audio configurations.
6. The company sells primarily to consumers and audiophiles, with historical installations in broadcast monitoring environments.
7. The organization's finished audio products are sold directly to end users and through consumer electronics retail channels.
8. The approach is distinguished by proprietary coaxial driver technology that co-locates tweeter and midrange drivers to improve acoustic imaging and directivity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company has collaborated with industrial designer Ross Lovegrove, partnered with consumer electronics brand Nothing, integrated Apple AirPlay 2 and is owned by GP Acoustics under the Gold Peak Group.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a larger consumer electronics and acoustics manufacturing group.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of finished audio products and optional physical accessories.
Scale and maturity: The organization was founded in 1961 and maintains a workforce of between 501 and 1,000 employees.
Geography: The company is based in Maidstone, United Kingdom and operates under a parent group headquartered in Hong Kong.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio products and acoustic engineering.

points.description: Chinese audio brand making affordable wireless earbuds and headphones with active noise cancellation and high-resolution sound.

1. An equipment maker that builds finished wireless earbuds and headphones running embedded firmware paired with a companion mobile application.
2. Acoustic transducers, active noise cancellation signal processing, and Bluetooth connectivity integrated into finished wearable hardware.
3. Dual-driver hi-res audio playback, adaptive active noise cancellation, AI-powered call clarity, multi-language real-time translation, and Auracast broadcasting.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products sold alongside a companion mobile software application.
5. Consumer earbuds, over-ear headphones, open-ear ear-clip devices, and Bluetooth speakers.
6. Consumers and budget-conscious retail buyers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end-users through online retail marketplaces.
8. The organization delivers feature-rich audio specifications, including dual drivers and Auracast, at sub-$100 price points.

points.name: Shokz
points.description: Consumer headphones manufacturer developing open-ear and bone conduction audio devices for sports and wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and sells consumer headphones specializing in open-ear and bone conduction audio devices for consumers, athletes, and outdoor enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker that builds consumer headphones and companion software sold as finished hardware worn by end users.
2. The core technology uses air conduction transducers and bone conduction transducers that send vibrations through the user's cheekbones directly to the inner ear, supported by audio algorithms for sound leakage reduction and bass optimization.
3. The organization delivers open-ear air conduction audio, bone conduction audio, multipoint Bluetooth pairing, and situational awareness while maintaining acoustic output in aquatic environments.
4. Customers get the technology as finished hardware devices and companion mobile applications.
5. The devices are used in running, swimming, commuting, office work, and general sports and fitness settings.
6. The organization sells directly to consumers.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to end users through retail channels and consumer electronics showcases.
8. The approach is distinguished by open-ear designs that prioritize situational awareness and safety alongside proprietary transducer mechanisms and ear-hook designs tailored for aquatic and athletic environments.

Scale and maturity: The company has sold over seven million headphone units across more than 60 countries and regions.
Geography: It is based in and operates across more than 60 countries and regions globally.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on consumer audio hardware and does not operate beyond the audio sector.

points.name: Dolby Laboratories
points.description: US technology company developing immersive audio formats for consumer devices.
points.bullets:
A technology and IP licensing company that develops proprietary audio and imaging formats, including object-based spatial audio, audio codecs, and noise reduction technologies, and licenses them to device manufacturers, content platforms, and automotive brands.
1. A technology and IP licensing company whose audio formats and codecs are embedded in partners' consumer electronics, automotive sound systems, and streaming platforms, alongside a secondary business selling finished cinema hardware.
2. Object-based spatial audio rendering algorithms, binaural HRTF processing, audio coding standards, and noise reduction algorithms, optimized to run on partner DSPs and cloud infrastructures.
3. Spatial audio rendering, binaural audio processing, audio encoding and decoding, noise reduction, and voice clarity for conferencing.
4. Licensed IP and algorithms integrated into partner hardware and software, finished cinema hardware, cloud post-processing APIs, and software plugins for digital audio workstations.
5. Cinemas, home theaters, PCs, smartphones, headphones, earbuds, soundbars, cars, gaming consoles, music and video streaming services, and professional audio mixing environments.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers, automakers, semiconductor companies, content platforms, film studios, streaming services, and cinema exhibitors.
7. Its audio formats and codecs are licensed to semiconductor vendors and device manufacturers for integration into consumer electronics, and to content platforms for media distribution.
8. It establishes proprietary audio formats as commercial standards across the entertainment industry through a combination of technology development, brand certification, and extensive patent licensing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Apple, BMW, Audi, LG, Samsung, TCL, Meta, Amazon, Netflix, Microsoft, Qualcomm, NXP, Cadence, Fraunhofer, and its subsidiary Via Licensing.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: IP and per-unit technology licensing, patent pool administration, hardware sales, and cloud API usage fees.
Scale and maturity: A large, established company founded in 1965 with fiscal 2025 revenue of USD 1.35 billion.
Geography: Based in San Francisco, California, USA, with a global presence across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific.
Beyond audio: It also develops and licenses imaging technologies, including high-dynamic-range video formats and video codecs.

points.name: Audioscenic
points.description: UK audio technology company developing user-adaptive 3D audio for gaming, automotive, and home devices.
points.bullets:
An audio IP licensor that develops spatial audio algorithms and licenses them to consumer electronics manufacturers for integration into loudspeaker-equipped devices.
1. An audio IP licensor whose spatial audio processing algorithms run on the digital signal processors inside consumer hardware products.
2. The core technology uses listener-adaptive position tracking, cross-talk cancellation algorithms, and beamforming on loudspeaker arrays to deliver independent audio signals to each ear through the air.
3. The specific audio capabilities delivered are user-adaptive 3D spatial audio rendering and cross-talk cancellation for binaural sound reproduction without headphones.
4. Customers get the technology through licensed software and algorithms integrated into their hardware.
5. The technology is used in soundbars, televisions, laptops, home cinema systems, PC gaming devices, console gaming setups, automotive audio systems, and public spaces.
6. The organization sells to consumer electronics brands and device makers.
7. Its licensed algorithms are integrated by device brands into finished consumer audio hardware.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by creating a personalized "virtual headphone" binaural experience over loudspeakers that continuously adapts to the exact moving position of the listener using head-tracking.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization partnered with a consumer electronics brand to integrate its spatial audio technology into a PC gaming soundbar.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: The company makes money through IP or software licensing and per-unit royalties.
Scale and maturity: The company has completed a Series A funding round, recently expanded its team, and is at an emerging growth stage.
Geography: The organization is based in Southampton, United Kingdom, and serves a global customer base.
Beyond audio: Audio technology is the organization's entire focus.

points.description: Japanese manufacturer building premium car audio systems and automotive infotainment components.
points.bullets:
An automotive audio equipment maker that designs and manufactures aftermarket and factory-installed infotainment systems, head units, speakers, subwoofers, amplifiers, and digital signal processors for vehicles. It builds premium high-resolution car audio systems and integration products for consumers, vehicle owners, and automakers.
1. A manufacturer of finished automotive audio hardware and infotainment systems sold as aftermarket components and integrated factory-installed modules.
2. Digital signal processing with ultra-low-phase-noise crystal clock management and automated sound tuning using calibrated microphones.
3. High-resolution 32-bit/384kHz audio playback, automated in-car acoustic correction, hands-free Bluetooth calling, and source integration for factory radios.
4. Finished hardware products including head units, subwoofers, amplifiers, audio processors, and connectivity hubs installed in vehicles.
5. Cars, automotive infotainment systems, aftermarket vehicle audio upgrades, and factory-installed sound systems.
6. Consumers, automotive enthusiasts, vehicle owners, and automakers.
7. Its audio components and systems are installed in vehicles through aftermarket retail channels and factory integration by vehicle manufacturers.
8. It targets high-resolution audio reproduction in vehicles through dedicated clock management systems and premium component-level integration.

points.description: Chinese technology company developing speech recognition and text-to-speech software.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer and software company that builds speech recognition, text-to-speech, translation, and large language models, finished smart hardware products, and SaaS applications for consumers, enterprises, and government agencies.
1. An AI model developer whose speech and language models run in the cloud behind APIs and services, and on-device in partners' chips, supplemented by a secondary business building finished consumer hardware.
2. Deep learning and neural networks for automatic speech recognition, natural language processing, text-to-speech synthesis, and large language modeling, running on cloud infrastructure and edge SoCs.
3. Speech recognition, text-to-speech synthesis, automated translation, speaker recognition, and natural language understanding across multiple languages and dialects.
4. Cloud APIs, software development kits, on-device software, SaaS subscriptions, and finished hardware devices.

points.name: Ableton
points.description: Berlin software company developing digital audio workstations for electronic music production and live performance.
points.bullets:
A developer of professional audio software and hardware that builds a digital audio workstation and a companion hardware controller, sold to electronic music producers and live performers.
1. A software and hardware maker whose digital audio workstation runs as desktop software on computers and whose controller is sold as a finished physical instrument.
2. The workstation combines non-linear clip sequencing, linear arrangement, time-stretching, MIDI sequencing, software synthesis and sampling, and object-based spatial mixing algorithms.
3. It delivers audio recording, MIDI sequencing, sound synthesis, audio time-warping, loop-based performance sequencing, and spatial audio mixing.
4. Customers get it as licensed desktop software products and finished hardware.
5. It is used in electronic music production studios and live performance rigs.
6. It sells to electronic music producers, live performers, and musicians.
7. Its software and hardware are used directly by musicians and producers to create and perform music.
8. Its non-linear session view and clip-based workflow make it the standard for live performance and electronic music production.

Key partners and customers: Its spatial audio workflow integrates with Dolby Atmos.
Organization type: It is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through tiered software licenses and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: It is an established company and an industry standard in its segment.
Geography: It is headquartered in Berlin, Germany, and operates globally.

points.bullets:
A developer tools and infrastructure company that builds an open-source framework and managed cloud services for developing, testing and deploying real-time voice AI agents, handling media transport, turn-taking and telephony for developers and enterprises.
1. A developer tools and real-time infrastructure company whose open-source framework and managed cloud services run in the cloud and on customer-hosted servers.
2. WebRTC media transport, selective forwarding unit routing and machine learning models for end-of-utterance turn detection and acoustic voice activity detection.
3. Real-time audio streaming, turn detection, adaptive interruption handling, telephony bridging, conversation recording and agent evaluation.
4. Open-source software frameworks, command-line tools, cloud application programming interfaces and managed WebRTC infrastructure services.
5. Call centers, conversational voice applications and automated telephony systems.
6. Developers, enterprises, artificial intelligence model developers and consumer technology brands.
7. Its framework and infrastructure are used by developers to build and deploy voice agents that integrate third-party speech-to-text, large language model and text-to-speech providers.
8. It provides a middleware orchestration layer and open-source framework that gives developers granular control over the voice agent pipeline rather than offering a closed managed platform or raw model application programming interfaces.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its notable partners and customers include OpenAI, Tesla, Spotify, Salesforce, xAI, Oracle, Twilio, Mistral AI, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Cartesia, Soniox, Telnyx and Index Ventures.
Organization type: A privately held venture-backed startup company.
Business model: Software-as-a-service subscriptions for managed cloud infrastructure with per-minute egress billing and commercial support for self-hosted deployments.
Scale and maturity: A unicorn-status company that recently raised one hundred million dollars in a Series C funding round at a one-billion-dollar valuation.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating globally.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on real-time communication infrastructure and voice agent tooling.

points.name: WellSaid Labs
points.description: Seattle AI software company generating synthetic voices for corporate training.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose neural text-to-speech and voice cloning models run in the cloud behind an API and a studio editor, providing licensed voice avatars and custom brand voices for enterprise professional audio production.
1. An AI model developer whose cloud-based neural voice models are accessed through a web studio application and real-time streaming APIs.
2. Large generative voice models trained on human voice recordings produce neural text-to-speech synthesis in the cloud.
3. The platform delivers studio-quality text-to-speech generation, voice cloning, pronunciation control, and emotional delivery direction.
4. Customers access the models through cloud APIs and a web-based software studio.
5. The technology is used in corporate training, e-learning, marketing materials, video ads, and enterprise communications.
6. The company sells to enterprises, Fortune 500 brands, and developers.
7. Its generated audio is exported and integrated by users into e-learning authoring tools and video editing platforms.
8. The approach emphasizes professional actor partnerships, strict data security with closed-model AI, and a comprehensive enterprise compliance portfolio.

Key partners and customers: Workflow integrations include Articulate, Camtasia, Waymark, Everlit, MNTN, and TRIPP.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: The company makes money through software platform subscriptions and API usage.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018, the company is an emerging player generating $8.3 million in revenue.
Geography: The company is based in Seattle, Washington, United States.

How it is delivered: Finished microphone components and silicon hardware, including analog, PDM, and I²S digital output microphones, as well as passive components like capacitors and inductors.
Used in: TWS earbuds, smartphones, smartwatches, smart glasses, AR/VR headsets, smart speakers, notebook PCs, security systems, automotive systems, and industrial devices.
Sells to: Consumer electronics brands, smart device makers, automakers, industrial equipment manufacturers, and edge AI processor designers.
Value chain: Its microphone components are designed into consumer electronics and IoT devices by product manufacturers and paired with edge AI processors.
Differentiator: It builds ultra-low-power, multi-mode digital microphones that integrate acoustic activity detection directly into the microphone hardware to support edge AI functions.

points.name: Orosound
points.description: Parisian startup developing AI-powered noise reduction technology for premium communication headsets.
points.bullets:
A maker of premium audio equipment and developer of AI-powered audio technologies. It builds finished headset hardware for professional communication and develops proprietary noise cancellation and voice enhancement algorithms, which it also licenses to chip companies.
1. An equipment maker that sells finished headsets and an AI model developer whose noise reduction and ANC algorithms run on partners' chips.
2. AI-based active noise cancellation algorithms, hybrid ANC and directional voice capture processing implemented on low-power processors.
3. Open-ear active noise cancellation, hybrid active noise cancellation, face-to-face conversation enhancement and directional voice recording.
4. Finished headsets sold to consumers and licensed IP or algorithms integrated by semiconductor vendors.
5. Office headsets, video conferencing, phone calls and open-ear audio devices.
6. Consumers, preorder backers and chip companies licensing the algorithms.
7. Its headsets are sold directly to end users and its algorithms are integrated by chip vendors into their processors.
8. It combines shipping its own finished open-ear and noise-cancelling headsets with licensing the underlying AI audio algorithms to semiconductor partners.

Business model: Hardware sales and IP or per-unit royalties.
Scale and maturity: A startup that raised crowdfunding in 2016 and was later acquired.
Geography: Based in Paris, France.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: AudioSourceRE
points.description: Irish startup developing AI software that isolates individual instruments and vocals from mixed audio recordings.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer and software developer that builds AI-powered sound separation and enhancement technology for professional audio applications, isolating vocals, instruments and speech from mixed recordings.
1. An AI model developer and software developer whose sound separation models run as desktop software and digital audio workstation plugins on users' computers, and are being ported to run on-device in embedded systems.
2. Machine learning models and spectral analysis algorithms process mixed audio recordings to isolate individual audio elements from complex sources.
3. The company delivers vocal extraction, instrument stem separation, drum removal, speech isolation, speaker identification and stereo field repositioning.
4. Customers get the technology as desktop software products, real-time plugins for digital audio workstations and licensed intellectual property for embedded systems.
5. The technology is used in music production studios, DJ setups, remixing workflows, hearing aids, automotive audio systems and consumer electronic devices.
6. The organization sells to producers, DJs, musicians, remix artists, chip companies, automakers and consumer device makers.
7. Its desktop software is used directly by audio engineers and producers, while its IP and models are integrated by chip vendors into their embedded platforms.
8. The approach combines over 20 years of dedicated source separation research with spectral analysis and machine learning models capable of real-time vocal extraction without cloud processing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It was acquired by Syntiant, partnered with GreenWaves to port its technology to the GAP9 processor, was spun out of Munster Technological University and received funding from Atlantic Bridge and Enterprise Ireland.
Organization type: The company is a spinout from Munster Technological University that operates as a subsidiary brand of Syntiant.
Business model: The organization makes money through software product sales, software licenses and intellectual property licensing.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018, the company raised a $2.1 million seed round and employs a leadership team with decades of specialized research experience.
Geography: Based in Cork, Ireland, the organization partners with international chip vendors, automakers and music applications in Asia.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio technology, with no operations outside the audio domain.

points.name: GreenWaves Technologies
points.description: French semiconductor startup designing ultra-low-power AI processors for hearable devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs ultra-low-power RISC-V application processors with neural network accelerators for AI inference and DSP in battery-powered edge devices, used by hearable and IoT device makers.
1. A fabless chip company that designs ultra-low-power RISC-V processors and neural network accelerators, sold as physical chips fabricated by third-party foundries and run on-device in consumer and industrial edge products.
2. A RISC-V processor cluster orchestrates a dedicated hardware neural network engine executing convolutions and multiply-accumulate operations at INT2, INT4 and INT8 precision, alongside a hardware sound filtering unit for autonomous time domain filtering.
3. The processors deliver on-device neural network inference for audio processing, enabling ultra-low latency adaptive noise cancellation, AI-powered sound elimination and enhancement, and keyword detection.
4. The company provides finished semiconductor chips, hardware development boards and a software development kit for code generation and neural network conversion.
5. The processors are designed into true wireless stereo hearables, wireless headphones, IoT sensor devices and automotive systems.
6. The company sells to hearable and IoT device makers, automotive suppliers and developers of edge audio and sensor software.
7. Its chips are designed into hearable and IoT products by consumer electronics brands and run third-party audio separation and noise reduction software licensed by IP providers.
8. The architecture is built on the open-source PULP platform and uses a sound filtering unit to reduce latency and power for audio processing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Foundry partners include GlobalFoundries for 22nm FD-SOI fabrication and TSMC for 55nm fabrication, with historical shareholder and investor backing from Thales, Soitec, Zepp Health, Innovacom and Bpifrance.
Organization type: A privately held startup that liquidated in 2025.
Business model: The company made money through chip sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2014, the company had 49 employees and reached volume production of its second-generation processor before liquidating in 2025.
Geography: The company was based in Grenoble, France.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus was on ultra-low-power processors for AI processing at the very edge.

points.name: Ambiq
points.description: US semiconductor company building ultra-low-power microcontrollers for AI and voice processing in edge devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that develops ultra-low-power microcontrollers and system-on-chips for edge AI applications, including on-device audio processing, for battery-constrained devices.
1. A chip company that designs low-power microcontrollers and system-on-chips that are sold as finished semiconductors running on-device at the edge.
2. The core technology is subthreshold power optimized transistor operation combined with Arm Cortex-M processors and neural processing units for on-device edge AI inference.
3. The specific audio capabilities it delivers include on-device neural network speech enhancement, speech de-noising, acoustic environment detection, wake words, and voice assistant integration.
4. Customers get it through chips and evaluation boards supported by software development kits, optimized AI runtimes, and a library of reference neural network models.
5. Its chips are used in smart rings, smart glasses, hearables, hearing aids, smartwatches, health monitors, and IoT devices.
6. The company sells to device makers and consumer electronics brands worldwide.
7. Its chips and accompanying software are designed into consumer electronics and wearable devices by product manufacturers.
8. Its approach is distinguished by its patented subthreshold power optimized technology platform that enables extreme energy efficiency for always-on edge inference.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is the first silicon licensee of the Cadence Tensilica HiFi 5 DSP, integrates Arm processors and NPUs, and its chips are supported by the Edge Impulse development platform.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: The company makes money through the sale of semiconductor chips.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2010, it has powered over 300 million shipped devices and operates at a large established commercial scale.
Geography: The company is based in Austin, Texas, USA, and supplies semiconductors to companies worldwide.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses on ultra-low-power semiconductor solutions for edge AI across healthcare, wearables, industrial automation, and smart environments, with audio as one application.

points.name: BrainChip
points.description: US semiconductor company building ultra-low-power neuromorphic processors for continuous always-on audio listening at the edge.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs neuromorphic processors and IP for processing audio at the extreme edge, providing reference SoCs, co-processors and licensable cores along with developer tools to device makers building always-on voice products.
1. A chip company that designs neuromorphic processors, sold as finished silicon and licensed IP that runs on customers' devices at the extreme edge.
2. Event-based neuromorphic networks implemented in hardware that process raw sensor data using spiking neural networks operating in the microwatt to milliwatt range.
3. Ultra-low-power wake word detection, voice command detection and continuous always-on listening.
4. The organization delivers its technology through physical chips, licensed processor IP cores, reference SoCs and software development kits.
5. Its processors are designed into smart appliances and wearables.
6. The company sells to device makers and chip companies.
7. Its chips and IP are integrated by device makers into always-on smart hardware products.
8. Its proprietary event-based neuromorphic architecture delivers standalone, ultra-low-power audio inference by triggering interrupts to wake main processors only when qualified events are detected.

Organization type: The company is a publicly traded company.
Business model: It generates revenue through a combination of IP licensing, silicon hardware sales and usage-based cloud service pricing.
Scale and maturity: The organization offers a range of commercialized processors and maintains established partnerships.
Geography: The company operates globally within the AI ecosystem.
Beyond audio: Its broader focus is on neuromorphic computing for artificial intelligence and sensor processing beyond audio.

points.description: Chinese component manufacturer producing acoustic parts like MEMS microphones for mobile devices.

A component manufacturer that designs and produces micro-acoustic components, including MEMS microphones, microspeakers, and haptic modules, for consumer electronics device makers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished acoustic and haptic components sold as hardware to device manufacturers.
2. Microelectromechanical systems, electromagnetic drives, and wafer-level packaging technologies used to build miniature acoustic transducers.
3. Audio capture via analog and digital MEMS microphones, audio reproduction via microspeakers, and tactile feedback via haptic actuators.
4. Finished hardware components, including microphones, speakers, and haptic modules, sold for integration into devices.
5. Smartphones, TWS earbuds, wearables, notebooks, tablets, automobiles, smart home devices, and gaming consoles.
6. Consumer electronics device manufacturers, automakers, and smart device brands.
7. Its components are designed into consumer electronic devices and automotive systems by global device brands.
8. Vertical integration of miniature acoustic components combined with high-volume precision manufacturing and in-house wafer-level packaging.

points.description: MEMS microphone manufacturer producing silicon microphones for consumer electronic devices.
points.bullets:
A silicon MEMS microphone manufacturer that produces CMOS-based acoustic sensors and packaged microphone components for consumer electronics makers.
1. A finished hardware component maker whose silicon MEMS microphone products are sold as packaged ICs and integrated into consumer electronic devices.
2. The core technology is CMOS-based MEMS acoustic sensing, using a diaphragm formed from a serpentine pattern in the CMOS metal layer combined with an integrated circuit containing a pre-amplifier and analog-to-digital converter.
3. The microphones deliver voice input quality, high-definition voice capture, and pulse density modulated or analog audio output with tight sensitivity matching.
4. Customers get the microphones as finished silicon components in surface-mount packages.
5. The microphones are used in consumer electronic devices including mobile phones, tablets, headsets, and small wearables.
6. The organization sells to consumer electronics device makers.
7. Its microphone components are designed into consumer electronic devices by consumer electronics brands.
8. It was the first company to produce a CMOS-based MEMS device, integrating the acoustic sensor and supporting circuitry using standard CMOS manufacturing processes.

3. The organization's audio components provide acoustic signal capture with specified signal-to-noise ratios for sound input in portable electronics.
4. Customers receive its products as finished hardware components.
5. Its components are used in handheld game players, mobile handsets, and medical equipment.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics brands, handset manufacturers, and gaming device makers.
7. Its packaged microphone components are designed into consumer electronics devices by OEMs and ODMs.
8. The organization focuses on packaging standard MEMS die sourced from semiconductor partners into branded components rather than designing its own MEMS die.

1. A component manufacturer that builds MEMS microphone and inertial sensor chips sold as packaged hardware for integration into electronic devices.
2. Capacitive micro-electro-mechanical systems fabricated using a patented wafer-level process, paired with CMOS technology and embedded firmware for signal processing and acoustic activity detection.
3. Acoustic capture with high signal-to-noise ratio, wide dynamic range, high acoustic overload point, ultra-low-power always-on keyword and voice command detection, and ultrasonic fingerprint sensing.
4. Finished hardware components, including digital I2S and PDM output microphones, analog output microphones, and PMUT-based ultrasonic sensors.
5. Smartphones, earbuds, smart glasses, AR/VR headsets, wearables, smart home devices, industrial tools, automotive systems, robotics, and IoT devices.
6. Consumer electronics device makers, automotive manufacturers, industrial equipment manufacturers, and acoustic component distributors.
7. Its microphone and sensor chips are designed into consumer electronics, automotive, and industrial hardware by device manufacturers.
8. Integrates an Acoustic Activity Detect feature directly into the microphone hardware to enable ultra-low-power always-on edge and generative AI voice triggering without requiring a separate codec.

points.description: US sensor company making piezoelectric MEMS microphones for wearable devices.
points.bullets:
A component maker that develops and manufactures piezoelectric MEMS microphones and voice accelerometers, selling robust acoustic sensors to consumer electronics brands and automotive manufacturers for voice interface applications.
1. A MEMS sensor company that designs piezoelectric acoustic transducers, sold as finished hardware components embedded in end-user devices.
2. Piezoelectric MEMS transducer technology, utilizing piezoelectric films and a no-back-plate architecture to convert acoustic waves and mechanical vibrations into electrical signals without standby power.
3. Acoustic sensing, acoustic wake-on-sound, bone-conduction voice pickup, tap detection, hardware voice activity detection, and high acoustic overload point capture.
4. Finished MEMS microphone and accelerometer hardware components.
5. Smart speakers, true wireless earbuds, headsets, hearables, smartphones, automotive cabins, industrial sensors, and outdoor devices.
6. Consumer electronics brands, automakers, acoustic module assemblers, and semiconductor companies.
7. Its MEMS microphones are designed into smart speakers, earbuds, and smart home devices by consumer electronics brands and selected for development kits by semiconductor vendors.
8. Its piezoelectric MEMS transducers draw nearly zero standby power for wake-on-sound functionality and use a backplate-free architecture that provides intrinsic resistance to water, dust, and shock.

Key partners and customers: Manufactured using GlobalFoundries and TSMC silicon wafers, assembled and tested by Unisem, packaged and sold in volume by AAC Technologies, selected for development kits by Synaptics, and funded by Amazon Alexa Fund, Bose, and American Family Ventures.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Component hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2014, based on technology originating from the University of Michigan, having raised $23 million to commercialize and scale mass production to hundreds of millions of units.
Geography: Based in Boston, Massachusetts, USA, operating globally through manufacturing and packaging partners.

points.name: USound
points.description: Austrian audio component company developing tiny MEMS speakers for hearables and wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
An audio component manufacturer that develops and produces piezoelectric MEMS microspeakers, audio amplifier ICs, and integrated audio modules for hearables and wearables.
1. A component manufacturer that builds piezoelectric MEMS microspeakers and amplifier ICs, sold as finished components and integrated modules for customer hardware.
2. Micro-electromechanical systems using piezoelectric actuators and PZT cantilevers to move an acoustic membrane, paired with application-specific integrated circuit amplifiers.
3. Silicon-based audio reproduction delivering high sound pressure levels, ultra-wide bandwidth up to 80kHz, low distortion, and energy recovery for power reduction.
4. Finished hardware components, microspeakers, amplifier ICs, and integrated reference designs delivered to device manufacturers.
5. TWS earbuds, hearing aids, smart glasses, virtual reality devices, and wearables.
6. Consumer electronics brands, ODMs, and hearing aid manufacturers.
7. Its microspeaker components are designed into hearables and earbuds by consumer electronics brands and ODMs.
8. Replaces traditional electrodynamic voice coil drivers with silicon-based piezoelectric MEMS technology to achieve radical miniaturization, reduced power consumption, and high production scalability.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named partners and customers include Luxshare-ICT, OBO Pro2, Soranik, Earweiss, QCY, Minami, ASE, Nordic Neuro Lab, Tiancheng, and Upstar.

Business model: Component and hardware sales.

It builds multi-channel hardware units incorporating third-party DSP chips and high-end digital-to-analog converters, offering advanced equalization, time alignment, and amplification for automotive sound systems.
1. An equipment maker that builds car audio DSP processors and integrated amplifiers, sold as finished hardware.
2. Digital signal processing hardware utilizing automotive-qualified SigmaDSP processors, 32-bit digital-to-analog converters, Class AB and Class D amplification stages, and Bluetooth audio codecs.
3. Parametric equalization with up to 31 bands per channel, crossovers, time alignment with fine step resolution, surround processing, and high-resolution digital audio playback.
4. Finished hardware units, including standalone processors and integrated amplifiers with multiple amplified and pre-amp output channels.
5. Car audio systems, including full active builds and competition vehicles.
6. Car audio installers and consumers, distributed through a US importer.
7. Its finished hardware is sold through importers and used in automotive audio installations by installers and enthusiasts.
8. It scales standalone and integrated DSP amplifiers up to 36 channels and 24 amplified channels for competition builds while incorporating high-end standalone digital-to-analog converters and built-in DSD players.

points.name: Airoha Technology Corp
points.description: Taiwanese fabless semiconductor company making Bluetooth audio chips for wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs low-power Bluetooth audio systems-on-chip for true wireless stereo earbuds and hearables, integrating application processors, DSPs, and reference audio software for consumer electronics brands.
1. A fabless chip company that designs low-power Bluetooth audio SoCs which are fabricated by a foundry and sold as physical integrated circuits running in customers' earbuds and hearables.
2. ARM Cortex-M4F application processors paired with Cadence Tensilica HiFi 5 DSPs and proprietary Bluetooth radio transceivers manufactured on a 12-nanometer low-power process.
3. Hybrid active noise cancellation, adaptive active noise cancellation, AI noise reduction, echo cancellation, and multi-microphone support.
4. Finished semiconductor chips shipped with software development kits and reference designs that include algorithms licensed from third-party audio software providers.
5. True wireless stereo earbuds, wireless headphones, smart speakers, assistive listening devices, and hearing aids.
6. Consumer electronics brands that manufacture earbuds and headphones.
7. Its chips are designed into true wireless stereo earbuds and headphones by consumer electronics brands.
8. Its proprietary MCSync transmission technology enables stable dual-ear wireless connections with low latency and balanced power consumption for high-resolution audio bitstreams.

Business model: Chip sales.

Geography: Based in Taiwan, selling to consumer electronics brands globally.

points.description: Kirkland, Washington standards organization defining Bluetooth specifications and overseeing wireless audio protocols.
points.bullets:
A standards body that defines Bluetooth wireless audio specifications, including the LE Audio standard, the LC3 codec and the Auracast broadcast audio feature, for consumer electronics and hearing aid manufacturers.
1. A standards body and trade association that develops wireless audio protocols and codecs, published as specifications that semiconductor and device companies implement in their chips and products.
2. Bluetooth wireless communication standards, including Bluetooth Low Energy radio protocols, the LC3 low-complexity communication codec and Auracast broadcast audio architecture.
3. Low-power wireless audio streaming, broadcast audio transmission to multiple receivers, multi-channel spatial audio playback and low-latency audio coding.
4. Published technical specifications, certification programs and trademark licenses.
5. Earbuds, hearing aids, smart speakers, public venues, airports, conference rooms and televisions.
6. Consumer electronics brands, hearing aid manufacturers, chip companies, automakers and software developers.

1. A fabless chip company that designs ultra-low-power wireless and audio SoCs and companion silicon, sold as packaged integrated circuits that run in customers' embedded devices.
2. Dual-core ARM Cortex-M33 processors running Bluetooth Low Energy stacks and LC3 audio codecs, integrated with neural processing units for hardware-accelerated edge AI inference.
3. Bluetooth Low Energy audio streaming, broadcast audio, low-latency wireless audio links, and on-device audio classification or keyword spotting using neural networks.

points.bullets:

3. Speech enhancement in noise, directional beamforming, feedback suppression, tinnitus masking, hearing aid fit verification, and direct audio streaming from phones, televisions, and public broadcast systems.
4. Finished wearable hardware, mobile applications, programming software, and companion streaming accessories.
5. Hearing aids, companion microphones, television streamers, and hearing care clinic fitting environments.
6. Hearing care professionals, clinics, distribution networks, government health services, and end consumers.

8. First to market with 2.4 GHz wireless technology, Made for iPhone compatibility, and Bluetooth LE Audio with Auracast broadcast audio in prescription hearing aids.

points.description: Software company building operating systems for smart headphones and earbuds.
points.bullets:

1. A developer tools and platform company whose operating system and development platform is licensed to headphone manufacturers to run on their devices.
2. An audio operating system that integrates wireless connectivity protocols, AI-driven audio processing, and a plugin architecture to host third-party applications on wearable devices.
3. Real-time spatial audio, head-tracking, dialogue enhancement, custom headphone profiles, wireless audio connectivity, and interaction with immersive media, environmental sound, and biometric data.
4. The operating system and development platform are provided as licensed intellectual property and software to device manufacturers.
5. Ear computers, hearables, earbuds, and headphones, including therapeutic hearing devices.
6. Headphone and earbud manufacturers, third-party application developers, and hardware brands.
7. Its operating system and platform are integrated by hardware manufacturers into their earbuds and headphones to serve end-users.
8. It creates an open, smartphone-style app ecosystem for ear-worn devices, allowing end-users to dynamically customize features rather than relying on fixed-function hardware.

points.bullets:

1. A developer of on-device audio AI models whose quantized neural networks run directly on customers' target edge hardware.
2. Computer vision architectures such as convolutional neural networks and transformer-based transfer learning applied to Mel spectrograms and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients derived from raw acoustic waveforms.
3. Acoustic anomaly detection for industrial assets, voice recognition, and environmental sound classification with background noise mitigation.
4. Edge-deployed machine learning models and specialized data science development services.
5. Industrial machinery, automotive in-car assistants, and customer support analytics systems.
6. Industrial organizations and enterprises requiring automated edge audio solutions.
7. Its models are developed and deployed directly onto the target edge hardware of its client organizations.
8. It specializes in engineering the path from microphone front-end features to efficient quantized models that run with low latency on local hardware rather than relying on cloud processing.

Beyond audio: Its focus is entirely on on-device audio artificial intelligence and the development of edge-deployable acoustic models.

points.name: Google AI Edge
points.description: US tech giant division building software tools to run artificial intelligence models directly on devices for real-time audio processing.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company and platform organization within Google that provides an integrated stack for building, optimizing and deploying on-device AI models for mobile and edge devices, including real-time audio processing. It supplies runtime frameworks, quantization tools, reference apps and libraries that let engineers run small language models and audio models locally under CPU and GPU constraints. The organization also ships demonstration apps that show on-device voice dictation, local transcription and voice-driven text editing.
1. A developer tools and platform company whose runtime, quantization and model-exploration tools engineers use to build and deploy AI models that run on-device at the edge on customers' hardware.
2. A suite of edge inference runtimes and on-device machine learning libraries, built around a lightweight tensor runtime with delegate-based hardware acceleration through integrated micro-kernels, that executes small language models and audio models on local CPU and GPU hardware.
3. Real-time on-device audio processing, local speech recognition, voice dictation, local transcription and voice-command text editing.
4. Software development kits, command-line tools, runtime libraries, reference applications and open-source model galleries distributed via model hubs.
5. Mobile and web platforms, desktop workflows and edge devices requiring local AI execution.
6. Developers, machine learning engineers and device makers building on-device AI applications.
7. Its runtime and optimization tools are used by developers to deploy open-source generative audio and language models onto edge hardware platforms.
8. It provides a vertically integrated on-device AI stack that couples a lightweight tensor runtime with automatic hardware acceleration via tightly integrated partner compute libraries.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Google as parent company, Arm, Stability AI and Hugging Face.
Organization type: A division of a publicly traded company.
Business model: Free open-source tools, libraries and reference applications provided as a platform for developers.

Geography: Based in Mountain View, California, USA, operating globally.

Analog summing of DAW stems, monitoring control with speaker switching and cue/talkback, stereo and surround monitoring up to Atmos, mid-side stereo width manipulation, analog routing and signal switching, shelving EQ, analog compression with dual-slope detection, and analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog conversion.

points.description: Industry association certifying wireless multichannel audio products for home theater.
points.bullets:

2. A wireless transmission protocol operating on DFS channels designed to broadcast, synchronize, and receive uncompressed, low-latency, high-resolution multi-channel digital audio.
3. Wireless transmission of up to 7.1 surround sound and 3D immersive audio formats, including Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, to up to eight active speakers without dropouts.
4. Licensed specifications, certification testing programs, and a technology brand applied to compliant finished hardware products manufactured by member companies.
5. Home theater systems, wireless speakers, audio/video receivers, and televisions.
6. Consumer electronics brands, speaker manufacturers, television manufacturers, and ecosystem partners.
7. Its specifications and certification programs are implemented by consumer electronics brands into interoperable wireless home audio products.
8. It provides a cross-industry standard specifically designed for low-latency, uncompressed multi-channel wireless audio, overcoming the multi-channel limitations of standard Bluetooth protocols.

4. Finished hardware products and companion software applications.
5. Consumer headphones, over-ear headphones, true wireless earbuds, and tethered Bluetooth earbuds.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to consumers through online campaigns, specialty retail stores, and regional distributors.
8. It measures ear-generated sound waves to create a personalized hearing profile and delivers it in a portable form factor at a lower price than comparable ear-scanning headphones.

Business model: Hardware sales of finished earbuds and headphones to consumers.

2. A combination of acoustic transducer hardware, wireless Bluetooth audio codecs, and on-device signal processing algorithms including adaptive active noise cancellation and deep neural networks.
3. The specific audio capabilities it delivers include adaptive active noise cancellation up to 50 decibels, personalized audio profiling, voice clarity processing, and high-resolution wireless audio playback.

2. Frequency and time domain audio encoding algorithms, three-dimensional spatial audio rendering standards, and miniaturized wireless body area network electronics.
3. Audio compression, immersive three-dimensional sound, speech enhancement, background noise reduction, and high-frequency perception enhancement for hearing aids.
4. Licensed intellectual property, patented audio standards, and developed microsystem hardware.
5. Mobile devices, televisions, automobiles, and hearing aids.
6. Technology developers, device manufacturers, and hardware engineers.

The organization serves automotive manufacturers, industrial vehicle builders, and professional audio integrators needing lightweight, low-latency local audio connectivity.

3. Multichannel audio transport, synchronous clocking distribution, power over cable, and I2C control data transmission across distributed nodes without requiring microcontrollers at slave endpoints.
4. Chips, licensed software stacks, and a graphical DSP development environment.

6. Automotive manufacturers, industrial vehicle equipment builders, and professional audio system integrators.

8. The networking technology combines audio, control, and power delivery over a single unshielded twisted pair cable while enabling slave nodes without microcontrollers, targeting local edge connectivity within 15-meter zones rather than competing with long-distance Ethernet protocols.

A standards organization that develops and publishes specifications for mobile telecommunications, including speech and audio codecs such as AMR, EVS, and IVAS for network operators and device makers.
1. A standards body that develops specifications and reference software for mobile telephony audio codecs that run on mobile network infrastructure and consumer devices.
2. Audio compression algorithms and spatial rendering formats for conversational voice and audio services over cellular networks.
3. Narrowband and wideband speech coding, full-band audio coding, immersive spatial audio rendering, and metadata-assisted spatial audio for real-time communications.
4. Published technical specifications, technical reports, and reference software implementations for standardized codecs.
5. Mobile telephony, 5G network voice and video calls, multi-stream teleconferencing, and AR/MR content streaming.
6. Mobile network operators, telecommunications equipment vendors, chip companies, and device manufacturers.
7. Its specifications are implemented by telecommunications equipment vendors and chip companies into network infrastructure and mobile devices.
8. It establishes globally mandated cellular telecommunications standards through a collaborative consensus process among competing industry players.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Ericsson, Nokia, Qualcomm, Samsung, Huawei, Fraunhofer IIS, VoiceAge, ETSI, NTT DOCOMO, Orange, Panasonic, ZTE, and Cadence.
Organization type: A collaborative standards development organization and ETSI partnership project.
Business model: Standardization processes funded by member organization contributions.
Scale and maturity: A global standards body with specifications deployed across worldwide cellular networks over multiple generations of mobile technology.
Geography: A global initiative with a global operational scope.
Beyond audio: It provides complete system specifications for cellular telecommunications network technologies beyond audio.

points.description: South Korean research division developing spatial audio formats and immersive audio codecs for consumer devices.
points.bullets:
A corporate research division that develops spatial audio metadata, encoding systems, playback architecture, and efficient room simulators for immersive audio formats.
1. A research and development organization whose audio processing algorithms and format architectures are integrated into consumer electronics hardware.
2. Immersive audio codecs, spatial rendering algorithms, and room simulation implementations form the core technology.
3. The organization delivers spatial audio rendering, format encoding, and device-compatible playback.
4. Customers and internal product groups receive the technology as licensed IP and algorithms integrated into hardware.
5. The technology is used in over-the-top streaming environments, live venues, and consumer electronics devices.
6. The organization primarily supports internal hardware divisions and collaborates with industry standards bodies.
7. Its research and architectures are standardized and integrated into consumer electronics by device manufacturers.
8. The organization co-develops open immersive audio standards rather than proprietary closed ecosystems.

points.name: Sonus faber
points.description: Italian high-end speaker manufacturer handcrafting luxury loudspeakers for home audio and cars.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of high-end loudspeakers and audio systems that handcrafts passive speakers, active wireless systems, subwoofers and all-in-one systems for audiophile consumers and luxury automotive brands.
1. An equipment maker that designs and builds finished loudspeakers and audio systems sold as physical hardware for home and car use.
2. Passive and active loudspeaker designs using custom drivers, silk dome tweeters, paper fiber cones, class-D amplification and room acoustics correction in sealed and ported cabinets.
3. High-fidelity music reproduction, multi-channel home theater sound, wireless active playback, bass extension and room correction.
4. Finished hardware sold as passive speakers, powered wireless speakers, subwoofers and integrated all-in-one systems.
5. Home listening rooms, home theaters and in-car audio systems for luxury cars.
6. Audiophile consumers, home theater enthusiasts and luxury automakers.
7. Its finished speakers are sold to consumers through distributors and dealers and integrated into luxury cars by automakers.
8. Distinguishes its products through Italian craftsmanship, lute- and violin-inspired cabinet aesthetics and natural sound drawn from classical instrument design.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with Maserati, Lamborghini and Pagani for in-car audio, with distribution handled by Synergy Audio Visual, and is owned by Bose as part of a luxury audio business unit.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand within a corporate portfolio, formerly part of McIntosh Group and acquired by a larger parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished loudspeakers and audio systems to consumers and automotive partners.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1983 with a global distribution footprint spanning Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, the UK and the US, and a product range spanning entry-level to flagship systems priced at hundreds of thousands of dollars.
Geography: Based in Italy with a global presence through international distributors.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is audio hardware design and manufacturing.

points.name: Orka
points.description: Chinese hearing technology company making AI-powered hearing aids that track health metrics and stream audio.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer healthcare wearables and finished hearing aid hardware that embeds proprietary AI audio processing and biometric sensors, targeting consumers with hearing loss.
1. A finished hardware maker whose hearing aids are sold as FDA-cleared Class II medical devices that run on-device in the ear.
2. Embedded AI and machine learning algorithms process audio and sensor data on the hearing aid hardware.
3. The devices deliver adaptive noise suppression, speech enhancement, health metric monitoring, Bluetooth audio streaming and hands-free calling.
4. Customers get the technology in finished, rechargeable wireless earbud-style hardware.
5. The products are used in hearing aids and consumer health wearables.
6. The organization sells directly to consumers.
7. Its finished hearing aids are sold to consumers through a technology partnership with an audio brand.
8. The core differentiator is the combination of FDA-cleared hearing aid functionality, active noise cancellation and biometric health monitoring in a single consumer wearable.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A notable partner is Bose, with which it co-developed and launched a noise-canceling hearing aid.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: The company makes money through finished hardware sales of its medical devices.
Scale and maturity: Founded in Silicon Valley in 2018, the organization is an award-winning consumer technology company.
Geography: The company was founded in Silicon Valley and operates globally, including in China.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the company builds healthcare wearables that use sensors to monitor health metrics like heart rate and step count.

points.name: Alliance for Open Media (AOMedia)
points.description: Standards consortium developing royalty-free open media specifications for spatial audio, including the IAMF format and Open Audio Renderer.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops open, royalty-free media specifications and reference implementations for spatial audio, providing interoperable foundations for developers.
1. A standards body that develops open media specifications and reference software for spatial audio, distributed as royalty-free open standards.
2. The core technology consists of spatial audio packaging specifications and rendering algorithms that support channel-based, scene-based, and object-based audio representations.
3. It delivers capabilities for packaging immersive audio content and rendering it for loudspeaker configurations and binaural headphone playback.
4. Customers get it through published open specifications and reference implementations offered under royalty-free terms.
5. The specifications are used in streaming, communications, gaming, extended reality, automotive, and wearable devices.
6. The organization provides its specifications to developers and technology companies across the industry.
7. Its open specifications and reference implementations are adopted by device makers and platform providers to build spatial audio products.
8. It distinguishes itself by offering open, royalty-free alternatives to proprietary, licensed spatial audio technologies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Netflix, NVIDIA, and Samsung, along with a design win for Samsung's Eclipsa Audio built on its specification.
Organization type: The organization is a non-profit standards consortium.
Business model: It operates without generating revenue from product sales or licensing fees, distributing its specifications under royalty-free terms.
Scale and maturity: The consortium is backed by nearly 50 global technology companies collaborating to drive industry-wide adoption.
Geography: It operates on a global scale with backing from major international technology companies.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the organization develops open, royalty-free media specifications across the broader media technology stack.

points.name: International Telecommunication Union
points.description: UN agency establishing broadcast audio standards for loudness measurement and immersive sound.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops and issues international recommendations and open standards for telecommunications and broadcasting, including specifications for immersive audio, audio loudness measurement, telephony speech coding, and speech quality assessment.
1. A standards body that publishes technical specifications and recommendations defining audio formats, measurement algorithms, and codecs for use by broadcasters, equipment makers, and telecommunications providers.
2. Standardized algorithms and file formats for object-based spatial audio, loudness and true-peak measurement, digital telephony speech coding, and objective speech quality assessment.
3. Immersive object-based spatial audio, audio programme loudness measurement, true-peak audio level measurement, wideband speech quality assessment, and digital telephony speech encoding.
4. Open standards, technical recommendations, and reference datasets published for implementation by industry stakeholders.
5. TV broadcasting, digital telephony, telecommunications networks, and audio programme exchange.
6. Broadcasters, telecommunications providers, equipment manufacturers, and standards-implementing organizations.
7. Its standards are implemented by equipment manufacturers and adopted by broadcasters and telecommunications providers in their production and distribution workflows.
points.profile:
Organization type: A specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for information and communication technologies.
Geography: Based in Geneva, Switzerland, and operating globally.

points.name: ITU
points.description: Global standards body setting audio loudness measurement standards for broadcasting and streaming.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops and maintains global Recommendations for information and communication technologies, including audio loudness measurement and broadcasting transmission frameworks, for the global broadcasting industry, national governments, and technology developers.
1. A standards body whose technical specifications are published as formal Recommendations adopted by industry participants.
2. Loudness measurement descriptors using K-weighting relative to full scale, and overarching telecommunications guidelines for analog and digital audio broadcasting transmission.
3. Uniform audio loudness measurement and standardized frameworks for analog, digital, and satellite audio broadcasting transmission.
4. Published technical standards and Recommendations that industry participants adopt.
5. Broadcast radio, television, streaming media, digital audio broadcasting, and satellite radio.
6. National governments, the global broadcasting industry, and private technology developers.
7. Its standards serve as the foundational interoperability layer adopted by broadcasters and equipment manufacturers.
8. It operates as a neutral United Nations arbiter rather than a for-profit commercial entity, establishing foundational compliance guidelines without competing in the product market.

Organization type: A specialized United Nations agency and standards body.

Scale and maturity: A global specialized agency of the United Nations.

1. A software company whose automated audio processing and mastering system runs as a software product in broadcast and post-production pipelines.
2. Audio processing algorithms and metadata embedding frameworks that render object-based audio into channel-based deliverables and manage immersive audio streams.
3. Automated mixing, object-based audio rendering, audio encoding, up-mixing, quality control, and automated language detection.
4. Software products and modular software tools.
5. Broadcast workflows, post-production pipelines, and content delivery.
6. Content creators and distributors.
7. Its software is integrated into broadcast and post-production pipelines by content creators and distributors.
8. Its system combines automated audio rendering, encoding, quality control, and language detection into a single automated workflow solution for post-production.

Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.

points.name: USL Inc.
points.description: Nevada audio equipment manufacturer building automated sound testing and signal processing tools for cinemas.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and test-and-measurement products that designs and manufactures audio-visual test devices, audio signal processors, and digital cinema processors for motion picture exhibition venues.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished hardware sensors, digital cinema processors, and accompanying diagnostic software for installation in cinemas.
2. Automated light and sound sensors with optical detection and Power over Ethernet, digital cinema processors, and diagnostic software for speaker and amplifier fault identification.
3. Automated daily testing of cinema projection and sound equipment, audio signal processing, B-chain processing, and diagnostic measurement of speaker and amplifier problems.
4. Finished hardware sensors, digital cinema processors, digital-to-analog converters, and specialized diagnostic software options.
5. Cinema auditoriums and motion picture exhibition venues.
6. Global cinema operators and exhibitors.
7. Its finished test-and-measurement equipment and cinema processors are installed directly in cinema auditoriums by exhibition operators.
8. Six-time winner of the International Cinema Technology Association Manufacturer of the Year award, recognized for engineering quality and customer support in the cinema exhibition sector.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired by and operates as a subsidiary brand of QSC, complementing its portfolio of cinema power amplifiers, signal processing, and loudspeakers.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a privately held professional audio company.
Business model: Hardware and equipment sales, including the direct design, manufacture, and sale of specialized test devices, processors, and accompanying software to cinema operators.
Scale and maturity: An established equipment manufacturer with products installed in over 5,000 cinema auditoriums, operating since its acquisition in 2016.
Geography: Based in the United States and serving global cinema operators.

points.description: Belgian technology company licensing immersive 3D audio formats for cinemas and home entertainment.
points.bullets:
An audio technology company that develops immersive 3D audio formats and object-based spatial audio technology, along with associated encoding tools and AV processors, for cinema, home entertainment, and professional audio markets.
1. An audio format and software developer whose spatial audio codecs and plugins run in studio production environments, cinema processors, and consumer AV receivers.
2. Channel-based and object-based spatial audio rendering algorithms that create three-dimensional soundfields with vertical height layers.
3. Immersive 3D audio playback, vertical sound reproduction, object-based spatial rendering, and multichannel audio encoding.
4. Licensed audio formats, software plugins, and AV sound processors.
5. Cinemas, home entertainment systems, professional studios, and live performance venues.
6. Content providers, consumer electronics brands, professional audio dealers, and studios.
7. Its formats are licensed to studios for content mastering and to consumer electronics brands for playback in AV receivers and processors.
8. It delivers a channel-based 3D audio format that adds a vertical height layer while remaining backward compatible with existing surround sound setups.

A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and sells high-end headphones, earphones and in-ear monitors, incorporating personalized sound technology based on ear scanning for consumers.
1. A consumer audio equipment maker that builds premium headphones, earphones and wireless earbuds sold as finished hardware worn by users.
2. Acoustic transducers and ear-scanning software are used to tailor frequency response to the individual listener's ear.
3. Personalized sound profiling based on ear scanning, high-fidelity audio reproduction and wireless audio reception.
4. The company delivers finished hardware and embedded software directly to end users.
5. Its products are used in personal entertainment, remote work, online learning and portable listening settings.
6. The organization sells directly to consumers.

points.name: Embody
points.description: California startup creating personalized spatial audio profiles from ear images.
points.bullets:
An AI model and software developer that builds personalized spatial audio applications and HRTF profiling technology for consumers, gamers, musicians and studios.
1. A software and AI model developer whose spatial audio and personalized HRTF applications run on consumer devices as installable apps and plugins.
2. Generative AI models analyze smartphone ear images to synthesize personalized head-related transfer function profiles, combined with spatial rendering and binaural decoding algorithms.
3. Personalized HRTF generation, spatial audio rendering, binaural monitoring, and in-game spatial sound awareness with visual overlays.
4. Standalone iOS applications, VST plugins for digital audio workstations, and spatial audio software for PC gaming headsets.
5. Games, music production, extended reality, professional studio mixing, and consumer headphones.
6. Consumers, PC gamers, musicians, audio engineers, and headphone manufacturers.
7. Its spatial audio software and HRTF technology are integrated into consumer headphones by hardware partners and distributed directly to end users as applications and plugins.
8. It generates individualized spatial audio profiles from user smartphone ear images rather than relying on generic HRTF measurements.

Geography: Based in San Mateo, California, USA.

points.name: Mimi Hearing Technologies
points.description: Berlin technology company personalizing sound based on individual hearing profiles.
points.bullets:
A software and AI model developer that builds sound personalization, hearing test, and neural audio codec technologies for consumer electronics brands and AI speech model developers. It licenses algorithms and models that adapt audio output to individual hearing profiles, and it develops a low-latency neural audio codec used by cloud-based voice AI. The organization has collected a large database of digital hearing profiles to power its personalization engines.
1. A software and AI model developer whose sound personalization algorithms run on-device in consumer electronics products and whose neural audio codec runs in the cloud behind speech models.
2. Digital hearing test algorithms, hearing-profile-based audio processing, and a transformer-based neural audio codec that distills self-supervised speech representations for low-bitrate audio streaming.
3. Sound personalization, hearing assessment, dialogue and voice clarity enhancement, background noise reduction, and neural audio compression.
4. SDKs, APIs, cloud models, and licensed algorithms integrated into consumer devices, plus mobile hearing test applications.
5. Earbuds, headphones, smartphones, televisions, soundbars, automotive sound systems, smart glasses, in-flight entertainment systems, browser extensions, and cloud-based conversational voice models.

points.name: International Telecommunications Union
points.description: International standards organization developing broadcast recommendations for measuring audio loudness levels.
points.bullets:

1. A standards body whose primary outputs are published technical recommendations, reports, and handbooks that define audio measurement algorithms and acoustic practices.
2. Defined algorithms for measuring audio programme loudness and true-peak audio levels, alongside specified practices for room acoustics.
3. Audio programme loudness measurement, true-peak audio level measurement, and room acoustics evaluation.
4. Published technical recommendations, reports, and handbooks adopted by the international community.
5. Broadcasting and telecommunications systems.
6. National regulators, broadcast organizations, and commercial audio equipment manufacturers and software developers.
7. Its technical recommendations are implemented by commercial audio equipment manufacturers and software developers to build compliant test and measurement tools.
8. It operates exclusively in the standards and licensing layer of the audio stack as a non-commercial specialized agency of the United Nations rather than as a manufacturer.

Geography: It operates globally as an international organization.
