2. Loudness measurement and normalization algorithms and parameters based on Programme Loudness targeting and true peak ceiling metrics.
3. Audio loudness normalization, loudness metering and loudness range measurement.
4. Open standards, technical guidelines and test signals.
5. Television and radio broadcasting, digital streaming platforms and media player software.
6. Public service broadcasters, audio product manufacturers and software developers.
7. Its standards are implemented by broadcasters in production workflows and by audio product manufacturers in measurement tools.
8. It serves as a central collaborative authority that shifted the European broadcast industry from peak normalization to loudness normalization to eliminate audience irritation from audio level jumps.

points.bullets:
A developer of professional audio software that builds spatial audio generation and sound design tools for post-production, film, television, games, and music production. The company creates native 3D audio software and spatial synthesizers that let users generate and manipulate thousands of simultaneous sounds in a virtual space using object-based audio and personalized binaural monitoring.
1. A software developer whose spatial audio tools run as desktop applications on users' computers.
2. CGI-like audio software using particle-based sound generation in 3D virtual spaces, integrating Higher Order Ambisonics, object-based audio rendering, and a spatial audio synthesis engine with MIDI-controlled spatial panning.
3. Spatial audio generation, particle-based sound design, binaural monitoring, Higher Order Ambisonics encoding, Dolby Atmos support, ADM object exporting, and spatial sound synthesis.
4. The software is delivered as perpetual software licenses for professional and enterprise tiers.
5. Post-production workflows for cinema, television, games, VR, and music production.
6. Studios, sound designers, mixing engineers, musicians, and producers.
7. Its software is used by audio post-production professionals in major film and television studios to create spatial soundscapes and object-based mixes.
8. It combines particle-based spatial audio generation with native spatial sound synthesis, allowing per-note spatial panning directly inside a synthesizer rather than relying on external 3D panners.

points.description: UK AI company developing generative music models and APIs for audio creation.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose generative audio models run in the cloud behind an API and on-device on consumer hardware. It builds text-to-audio models, a low-bitrate speech codec, and audio editing tools that generate music, loops, stems, and sound effects from text prompts for music professionals and enterprises.
1. An AI model developer whose audio and codec models are sold as cloud APIs and open-weight models running in the cloud and on-device on consumer hardware and mobile devices.
2. Continuous latent diffusion models and transformer-based diffusion architectures generate audio from text prompts, while a transformer-based variational autoencoder and a discrete token codec handle audio encoding and watermark embedding.
3. The models generate full-length musical tracks, instrumental loops, stems, sound effects, ambient sounds, and foley recordings, and apply style transfer, audio-to-audio transformation, and inpainting.
4. Customers access the models through open-weight model downloads, cloud APIs, a web application, and a plugin for digital audio workstations.
5. The models and software are used in professional music production studios, enterprise sound production pipelines, and consumer mobile devices.
6. The company sells to music professionals, enterprises, developers, and consumer hardware users.
7. Its open-weight models are downloaded and integrated by developers and music professionals, while its cloud models are hosted by cloud platforms and accessed via API.
8. It trains its models on fully licensed music catalogs and Creative Commons recordings screened for copyright, and provides open weights under a community license with required enterprise licenses for commercial use by high-revenue entities.

points.description: Software framework building cross-platform audio applications and plugins.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides an open-source C++ software framework used by developers to build audio plugins and applications for desktop and mobile operating systems.
1. A developer tools company whose platform engineers use to build cross-platform audio plugins and applications compiled into standard plugin formats that run in digital audio workstations.
2. A C++ application framework with classes for audio DSP, MIDI processing, and GUI development, featuring sample-accurate parameter automation, a clear separation between GUI and audio threads, and project management tools.
3. It enables the development of custom audio DSP, software synthesizers, MIDI processors like arpeggiators, noise gates, and multi-channel surround monitors.
4. It is provided as a software framework distributed under open-source and commercial licenses, including project configuration tools and educational courses.
5. It is used to build virtual studio instruments and effects that run in digital audio workstations on desktop and mobile devices.
6. It is used by audio software developers, amateur programmers, and music technology companies building plugins and audio applications.
7. Its framework is used by audio software companies to build commercial plugins and applications for end-users.
8. It allows a single codebase to be compiled across all major desktop and mobile operating systems and plugin formats, dominating audio plugin development over competing open-source frameworks.
points.profile:

Organization type: It is a partially open-source software project and framework with commercial licensing options.

Geography: It operates globally as a software framework and digital product.

The organization develops neural network models for speech recognition, audio synthesis, and audio language modeling, providing enterprise-grade infrastructure and tools for developers and businesses.
1. An AI model developer and cloud computing provider whose speech and audio models run in the cloud behind APIs, alongside a managed machine learning platform that engineers use to build and deploy ML models.
2. Deep learning neural networks and large generative models, including decoder-only Transformers for audio language modeling, neural audio codecs for acoustic tokenization, and self-supervised speech representation models for semantic tokenization.
3. Speech recognition, text-to-speech synthesis, voice cloning, multi-speaker diarization, streaming transcription, and generative audio synthesis for speech and music.
4. Cloud APIs, SDKs, client libraries, and a managed machine learning platform.
5. Contact centers, conversational AI agents, in-vehicle voice experiences, call center automation, audiobooks, and video voice-overs.

8. Its deep integration with a broader cloud ecosystem and a proprietary AI research division provides enterprise-grade compliance, data residency, and a managed platform for end-to-end conversational AI development.

6. The company sells to audio engineers, system integrators, and installation professionals.
7. Its finished amplifier hardware is integrated into installed audio systems by system integrators.
8. Up to 32 configurable input and output channels packed into a single rack unit using gallium nitride technology distinguish its dense amplifier designs.

A manufacturer of professional guitar effects pedals that builds premium digital and analogue audio products, including delay, reverb, modulation, overdrive, and compressor pedals, for guitarists and producers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished guitar effects pedals and studio-quality rack processors that run as standalone hardware stompboxes.
2. The core technology combines digital signal processing using SHARC chips operating at a 96kHz sample rate with proprietary algorithms for tape delay emulation and analog delay recreation, alongside all-analogue audio circuits.
3. The hardware delivers specific audio capabilities including delay, reverb, modulation, overdrive, and compression effects.
4. Customers get the effects as finished hardware pedals and rack processors.
5. The devices are used in guitar signal chains, live performances, and recording studios.
6. The company sells directly to musicians, producers, and touring artists.
7. Its finished hardware pedals are placed directly in the audio signal chains of end-user musicians.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by combining high-fidelity digital signal processing chips with proprietary algorithms to emulate analog and tape effects within stompbox form factors.

points.description: California manufacturer making guitar strings, instruments, and effects pedals.
points.bullets:

2. Analog and electronic audio hardware components, including string winding, passive volume control, expression pedal mechanisms, and isolated DC power circuitry.
3. Guitar tone generation, signal volume control, delay effect generation, and pedalboard power distribution.

5. Its products are used in live music venues, recording studios, and by individual guitarists on pedalboards.
6. The organization sells to musicians and retail music stores.
7. Its finished goods are distributed through retail networks directly to musicians.
8. The organization differentiates itself through a legacy of string manufacturing and custom-gauge offerings, coupled with an expansion into premium effects pedals through brand acquisition.

points.name: TONE3000
points.description: US software company hosting guitar amplifier models and providing integration tools for audio hardware.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer and platform company that develops open-source neural amp modeling technology and maintains a large library of community-generated captures and impulse responses for guitarists and bassists.
1. An AI model developer whose neural network amp models and capture library are provided as free open-source plugins for desktops and embedded hardware, alongside an API for hardware integration.
2. Neural networks using dilated convolutions that model the sound of analog amplifiers and effects, trained on audio recordings and designed to run on low-power ARM microcontrollers or host CPUs.
3. Neural amp modeling, impulse response loading, signal chain building, dual chain routing, and tone capture training and distribution.
4. Free open-source plugins, an API for hardware integration, a web platform for model distribution, and embedded software variants for consumer hardware.
5. Multi-effects pedals, practice amps, bass amplifiers, studio software, and web browsers.
6. Consumers, guitarists, bassists, and instrument amplifier and effects hardware manufacturers.
7. Its neural models and capture library are integrated by consumer electronics brands into their multi-effects pedals and amplifiers.

points.description: US pro audio company building guitar multi-effects processors and amp modelers.
points.bullets:

1. A hardware maker whose floorboard multi-effects processors and amp modelers run on dedicated DSP engines in finished physical devices.
2. Multicore DSP engines running hundreds of amp, cabinet, microphone, and effects models, alongside integrated open-source machine learning architectures for on-device neural amp modeling.
3. Guitar and bass amp modeling, cabinet simulation, effects processing, audio cloning, USB audio interfacing, wireless rig management, and tone sharing.
4. Finished hardware units, companion desktop software, and cloud platforms.
5. Live performance rigs, recording studios, and home practice setups for guitarists and bassists.
6. Budget-conscious musicians, guitarists, and bassists.
7. Its finished hardware devices are sold directly to musicians for live and studio use.
8. It integrates open-source neural amp modeling architectures directly into its touchscreens for on-device use without a computer, offering statistically proven modeling at accessible price points.

points.description: Audio equipment manufacturer building compact touchscreen multi-effects units for guitarists.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures compact, touchscreen-driven floorboard multi-effects units, digital amplifiers, and effects pedals for musicians. It builds guitar amp modelers, multi-effects processors, and reverb pedals incorporating proprietary DSP modeling and convolution technologies. The company sells finished hardware products to guitarists and bassists seeking tone-shaping and amplification tools.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware products, specifically compact floorboard multi-effects units and pedals, sold as physical devices that run their internal DSP and modeling software on dedicated embedded processors within the hardware.
2. The core technology comprises digital signal processing systems utilizing proprietary modeling algorithms, convolution reverb engines, and firmware designed to run embedded neural amp modeling formats on the device hardware.
3. It delivers guitar amplification modeling, multi-effects processing, convolution reverb with impulse response support, and expression pedal control for audio signal chain manipulation.
4. Customers receive the technology as finished physical hardware units, including floorboard multi-effects processors, compact digital amplifiers, and effects pedals, sold with embedded firmware and editor software.
5. The products are used in live stage performance, studio recording, home practice setups, and pedalboard signal chains for guitar and bass.
6. The company sells directly to musicians, including guitarists and bassists, as end consumers of its hardware.
7. As a finished equipment maker, it occupies the final product tier, selling branded hardware directly to musicians, integrating internal DSP and mechanical components designed in-house.
8. Its approach is distinguished by combining feature-rich multi-effects processing and modeling capabilities into compact, budget-friendly hardware formats with touchscreen interfaces.

points.description: German audio manufacturer capturing the exact sound of physical guitar amplifiers into digital devices.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds digital hardware devices for guitar amplifier profiling and simulation. It captures the exact sonic characteristics of physical amplifiers using test tones and impulse responses, providing tone-sculpting tools, DSP effects, and routing capabilities for musicians and audio professionals.
1. An equipment maker that builds standalone digital signal processing hardware units in the form of heads, rack units, and floorboards.
2. Patented profiling technology running on ARM processors that sends test tones into physical amplifiers to capture their exact sonic characteristics using over 100,000 individual frequency points and impulse responses.
3. The devices deliver exact amplifier profiling, cabinet and microphone simulation, and integrated DSP effects processing.
4. Customers get the technology as finished premium hardware units supplemented by free ongoing software updates.
5. The devices are used by guitarists and audio professionals in studios and live performance settings.
6. The organization sells directly to musicians, sound enthusiasts, and audio professionals.
7. Its finished hardware units are purchased directly by end users for use in live and studio audio rigs.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by creating an exact, physics-rooted copy of a specific amplifier's settings rather than a generalized approximation.

A manufacturer of measurement microphones and audio measurement systems for recording and loudspeaker measurement applications. It builds calibrated reference microphones and measurement hardware used to generate and record audio signals in anechoic chambers. Its products are used by engineers and acousticians for loudspeaker measurements and recording work.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment that builds measurement microphones and hardware measurement systems sold as finished hardware.
2. The core technology comprises omnidirectional microphone capsules with flat frequency responses and hardware systems for generating and recording audio signals at high sampling rates.
3. It delivers calibrated, flat-frequency-response audio capture and signal generation for loudspeaker measurement and recording.
4. Customers get its products as finished hardware.
5. Its products are used in anechoic chambers, recording studios and loudspeaker measurement setups.
6. It sells to engineers, acousticians and measurement professionals.
7. Its finished measurement hardware is purchased directly by acoustic measurement professionals and engineers.
8. It provides highly calibrated microphones with tight flat-response tolerances for measurement-grade applications.
points.profile:

Organization type: It was a privately held company that has gone bankrupt and been purchased from the bank.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of microphones and measurement systems.
Scale and maturity: It was a longstanding US audio company with US manufacturing that has ceased operations.
Geography: It is based in the US and manufactures in the US.

2. The measurement suite uses real-time analysis, sound level measurement, log swept sine and room response algorithms running on mobile devices, paired with calibrated measurement microphones.
3. The organization delivers real-time spectrum analysis, sound pressure level measurement, log swept sine analysis and room response measurement.
4. Customers get the offering as finished hardware microphones and as a software application installed on iOS devices.
5. The products are used in acoustic measurement, room analysis and audio system calibration.
6. The company sells to audio professionals, acousticians and system installers.
7. Its hardware microphones and software applications are used directly by end users for acoustic measurement and system calibration.
8. The organization pairs calibrated measurement microphones with an integrated iOS application that supports importing external calibration files.

points.name: Holoplot
points.description: Berlin pro audio manufacturer building 3D spatial sound systems for immersive experiences.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures matrix array sound systems for immersive sound reinforcement, and develops accompanying control and simulation software for audio system designers and integrators.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished loudspeaker arrays and audio modules, alongside proprietary control and simulation software that runs on standard computing hardware.
2. Wave Field Synthesis and 3D audio beamforming algorithms processing individual drivers in two-dimensional matrix arrays to create controlled sound fields and authentic spatial localization.
3. 3D sound field manipulation, multiple simultaneous sound field generation from single arrays, complete horizontal and vertical beam control, and authentic sound localization at high sound pressure levels.
4. Finished hardware loudspeaker modules and arrays, alongside proprietary software for system design, acoustic simulation, and operational control.
5. Large-scale immersive entertainment venues, permanent installations, and live events requiring spatial sound reinforcement.
6. Immersive experience operators, entertainment venue owners, event producers, and professional audio system integrators.
7. Its finished hardware and software are deployed directly into permanent installations and live event productions by venue operators and integrators.
8. It scales wave field synthesis technology to high sound pressure level applications through large matrix arrays of individually processed drivers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired by Sphere Entertainment, with measurement technology from Klippel, acoustic simulation software compatibility with AFMG EASE, and deployments for Nintendo and Illuminarium.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded entertainment company.
Business model: Hardware sales of loudspeaker arrays and modules, alongside associated software.
Scale and maturity: An established company with proven commercial deployments in large-scale global entertainment venues.
Geography: Based in Berlin, Germany, deploying systems in global entertainment markets.
Beyond audio: Audio is the sole focus of the organization.

points.name: HEAD acoustics
points.description: German acoustic engineering company developing measurement systems and analysis software for evaluating vehicle sound quality and voice communications.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and equipment company that provides hardware, software and simulation systems for measuring, analyzing and optimizing acoustics, vibration, speech and audio quality for device manufacturers and developers.
1. A developer tools and equipment maker whose test and measurement instruments and analysis software run in engineering laboratories and simulation environments.
2. Acoustic measurement and simulation systems using binaural artificial heads, data acquisition hardware and perceptual modeling algorithms.
3. Sound and vibration analysis, audio and speech quality assessment, acoustic environment and background noise simulation, and voice recognition performance testing.
4. Hardware data acquisition platforms, artificial heads, acoustic cameras, analysis software, simulation software and consulting services.
5. Automotive development, telephony, smart home devices, broadcast AV, staging and audio product development laboratories.
6. Device manufacturers, automotive suppliers and developers.
7. Its measurement and simulation tools are used by manufacturers and developers to test, benchmark and tune their audio products during development.
8. It provides holistic acoustic test environments that combine binaural recording hardware with software for objective, perception-based quality scoring.

Organization type: A privately held company.

Geography: Headquartered in Germany with subsidiaries in China, France, Italy, India, Japan, South Korea, the UK and the USA.

points.description: Boston technology company improving voice interfaces using AI to isolate human voices and identify speakers in noisy environments.

1. An AI software developer whose voice biometric and signal processing algorithms run on existing hardware without requiring dedicated additional audio components.
2. Signal processing and biometric voice profiling algorithms that identify a specific human speaker in noisy environments based on unique voice characteristics.
3. Noise suppression and voice identification based on the user's unique voice biometric profile.
4. Software algorithms licensed for integration into hardware platforms.
5. Automotive voice interfaces.
6. Automotive suppliers and manufacturers.
7. Its software is integrated by automotive suppliers and manufacturers into their vehicle platforms.
8. It isolates and identifies target human voices in noise using voice biometric profiles without requiring additional hardware.

points.description: US speaker manufacturer building acoustic suspension speakers and subwoofers for home theater systems.
points.bullets:

1. A consumer audio equipment maker whose finished loudspeaker and subwoofer hardware runs in home listening rooms.
2. Traditional acoustic suspension loudspeaker designs using matched dome tweeters, cone woofers and up-firing drivers.
3. Two-way and three-way sound reproduction, low-frequency bass extension and Dolby Atmos spatial audio elevation effects.
4. Finished passive and powered speaker hardware, including floor-standing, satellite, center-channel and add-on modules.
5. Home stereo systems and multi-channel Dolby Atmos home theater setups.
6. Consumers and home audio enthusiasts.
7. Its finished speakers are sold through consumer retail channels to end users.
8. It delivers high-performance acoustics using compact footprints and broad dispersion for home system builders.

points.description: Danish measurement technology company producing high-precision microphones, sound level meters, and audio analyzers for acoustic and vibration testing.

A manufacturer of professional audio and vibration measurement equipment that supplies precision microphones, sound level meters, analyzers, acoustic calibrators, head and torso simulators, and data acquisition software for acoustic compliance testing, research, and product development.
1. An equipment maker and software developer that builds finished acoustic measurement hardware and analysis software sold as laboratory instruments and application licenses running on dedicated hardware and PCs.
2. The core technology comprises precision acoustic transducers, analog front ends, head and torso simulators with realistic ear simulators, and modular data acquisition and analysis software.
3. The organization delivers high-precision sound pressure level measurement, frequency analysis, acoustic calibration, building acoustics measurement, hearing aid measurement, transducer measurement, and sound imaging.
4. Customers receive the offerings as finished hardware instruments, measurement microphones, test chambers, acoustic calibrators, and licensed software applications.
5. The products are used in acoustic laboratories, product development facilities, compliance testing facilities, building acoustics assessments, and consumer audio testing labs.
6. The organization sells to enterprises, research institutions, consumer electronics brands, acoustic test laboratories, and developers of audio measurement systems.
7. Its measurement instruments are used by device manufacturers and test labs to validate and develop audio products.
8. Its approach is distinguished by a long-established focus on high-precision Class 1 measurement standards and a comprehensive ecosystem of modular hardware and software built for acoustic analysis.

1. A professional audio equipment maker that designs and sells finished microphone hardware for laboratory-grade precision and professional audio applications.
2. The core technology is precision microphone design, including calibrated, omnidirectional electret condenser capsules engineered for a flat frequency response and uncolored sound capture.
3. It delivers high-clarity, low-noise sound capture with exceptional reliability and precise acoustic measurement capabilities for critical analysis.
4. Customers get finished hardware, premium measurement microphones, alongside calibration services and serialized calibration files.
5. The products are used in acoustic analysis, studio recording, broadcast, theater, and sound reinforcement environments.
6. Customers are audio professionals, including those performing on-location acoustic analysis, speaker driver output measurement, and whole-room response testing.
7. Its finished measurement microphones and calibration data are used directly by audio professionals and integrated into acoustic test and measurement workflows.
8. The approach is distinguished by the production of calibrated, flat-frequency-response microphones that offer pure, uncolored sound with unparalleled specifications.

points.description: Spanish manufacturer building loudspeakers and power amplifiers for professional sound reinforcement.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures loudspeaker cabinets and power amplifiers for professional sound reinforcement, providing finished hardware and setup software for live, touring, and installed sound environments.
1. An equipment maker that builds analog and Class D power amplifiers, loudspeakers, and configuration software sold as finished hardware and software products running in professional sound systems.
2. Analog and Class D amplifier electronics and loudspeaker cabinet acoustics, supported by acoustic simulation data formatted as GLL files for system design platforms.
3. Multi-channel sound amplification across a wide range of power outputs, and sound reinforcement for venues and live events using loudspeaker enclosures and subwoofers.
4. Finished hardware products, including power amplifiers and loudspeakers, plus system configuration software and acoustic simulation data files.
5. Live touring sound systems, installed sound in venues, sports competition audio, restaurants, and nightclubs.
6. Audio professionals, system integrators, installation contractors, and regional audio equipment distributors.
7. Its finished hardware is specified and installed by integration companies and distributors into professional sound reinforcement venues.
8. It supplies both the power amplification and the loudspeaker enclosures as finished hardware, accompanied by proprietary configuration software and acoustic simulation data for system design.

points.description: Berlin software company developing acoustic simulation tools for room and loudspeaker modeling.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds acoustic simulation and measurement software for sound system designers, acousticians and loudspeaker manufacturers.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation and measurement software runs as desktop applications on Windows PCs.
2. Geometric acoustic modeling, electroacoustic simulation and acoustic measurement algorithms.
3. Room acoustic modeling, loudspeaker behavior prediction, speech intelligibility prediction, coverage mapping and FIR filter generation.
4. Software products distributed through software licenses and activation keys, with a free simulation viewer and a database of loudspeaker data files.
5. Sound system design for venues, room acoustic simulations, line array configuration and acoustic measurement.
6. Acousticians, sound system designers, audio engineers, consultants, loudspeaker manufacturers and system integrators.
7. Its simulation software is used by consultants and system designers to model sound systems prior to installation in venues.
8. The company's software is a brand-agnostic industry standard for acoustic simulation, supported by a proprietary loudspeaker data format and a database of over 30,000 loudspeaker files.

points.name: COMSOL
points.description: Swedish software company developing multiphysics simulation tools used to model loudspeakers, microphones, room acoustics, and acoustic-structure interactions.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company whose simulation platform engineers use to model audio and acoustic devices and systems. The organization provides multiphysics simulation software for modeling sound waves and their interactions with solids and fluids, selling licenses for its core platform and add-on modules to hardware manufacturers and acoustic engineering consultants.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation platform engineers use to design, simulate and test acoustic and audio products.
2. The core technology is finite element method and multiphysics simulation software that calculates acoustic-structure interactions and vibroacoustics, incorporating hybrid FEM-ray tracing for room acoustics and GPU-accelerated solvers.
3. The platform delivers simulation and analysis of loudspeaker drivers, MEMS microphones, piezoacoustic transducers, automotive cabin acoustics, room and building acoustics, and sonar systems.
4. Customers get the capabilities through commercial software licenses for simulation tools and application server software for deploying custom-built simulation apps.
5. The tools are used in designing loudspeakers, MEMS microphones, automotive cabins, absorptive mufflers, smart speakers and building acoustics.
6. The organization sells to hardware manufacturers designing acoustic products and acoustic engineering consultants analyzing audio devices and environmental noise.
7. Its simulation software is used by hardware brands and engineering consultants to design and optimize acoustic transducers, audio devices and sound environments.
8. The approach is distinguished by integrated multiphysics capabilities that combine acoustic modeling with structural mechanics and fluid dynamics to calculate real-world vibroacoustic interactions.

Kind of provider: A developer tools company whose simulation platform engineers use to design, simulate and test acoustic and audio products.
Core technology: The core technology is finite element method and multiphysics simulation software that calculates acoustic-structure interactions and vibroacoustics, incorporating hybrid FEM-ray tracing for room acoustics and GPU-accelerated solvers.
Capabilities: The platform delivers simulation and analysis of loudspeaker drivers, MEMS microphones, piezoacoustic transducers, automotive cabin acoustics, room and building acoustics, and sonar systems.
How it is delivered: Customers get the capabilities through commercial software licenses for simulation tools and application server software for deploying custom-built simulation apps.
Used in: The tools are used in designing loudspeakers, MEMS microphones, automotive cabins, absorptive mufflers, smart speakers and building acoustics.
Sells to: The organization sells to hardware manufacturers designing acoustic products and acoustic engineering consultants analyzing audio devices and environmental noise.
Value chain: Its simulation software is used by hardware brands and engineering consultants to design and optimize acoustic transducers, audio devices and sound environments.
Differentiator: The approach is distinguished by integrated multiphysics capabilities that combine acoustic modeling with structural mechanics and fluid dynamics to calculate real-world vibroacoustic interactions.

2. Coaxial loudspeaker designs, passive cardioid sound dispersion technology, temporal equalization algorithms, and object-based immersive audio processing.
3. Sound dispersion control, directivity management, room acoustic correction, active acoustics, and object-based mixing.
4. The company sells finished hardware devices and software platforms for system design and simulation.
5. Performance spaces, sports venues, houses of worship, and public environments.
6. Audio professionals, system integrators, and venue operators.
7. Its loudspeakers and processors are installed in public venues by audio professionals.
8. The company integrates digital signal processing as a core design ingredient in its coaxial loudspeakers, using temporal equalization to improve real-world sound in difficult rooms.

Geography: Based in Whitinsville, Massachusetts, USA, with products deployed in venues worldwide.

2. Geometrical and hybrid modeling techniques, including ray tracing and wave propagation analysis, calculate room acoustic parameters and support head-related transfer functions.
3. Room acoustic prediction, reverberation time calculation, speech transmission index calculation, clarity measurement, sound pressure level calculation, and auralisation.
4. Software products sold as software licenses.
5. Classrooms, open-plan offices, and orchestral environments.
6. Acoustic consultants and architects.
7. Its simulation software is used by acoustic consultants and architects to design indoor spaces.
8. The software's accuracy is continuously validated against other commercial acoustic modeling tools through round-robin tests.

Geography: Based in Denmark.

points.name: Treble Technologies
points.description: Icelandic startup developing cloud-based acoustic simulation software for product design and AI training.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides a cloud-based acoustic simulation platform used by engineers to virtually prototype audio hardware and generate synthetic audio datasets for training and testing AI models.
1. A developer tools company whose acoustic simulation software and software development kit run in the cloud.
2. A cloud-native hybrid solver combining finite element and geometrical acoustics to simulate wave-based sound propagation, capturing diffraction, phase effects, and interference.
3. It delivers room impulse response generation, binaural spatial audio rendering, acoustic digital twins, and synthetic acoustic scene creation.
4. Customers access the simulation tools through a cloud-based web application and a Python software development kit.
5. The technology is used for virtual prototyping of wearables and smart glasses, architectural room acoustics, and generating training data for speech enhancement and noise suppression models.
6. The company sells to device manufacturers, audio hardware brands, acoustic engineering firms, and AI model developers.
7. Its simulation software and synthetic datasets are used directly by product engineers and AI researchers to design and validate audio hardware and voice models.
8. Its hybrid wave-based solver computes complex acoustic phenomena up to 100 times faster than conventional methods while maintaining physically accurate results across the full frequency spectrum.

Key partners and customers: Notable partners and customers include Amazon, Logitech, Jabra, L-Acoustics, Arup, Saint-Gobain, Spatial, and investors such as Paladin Capital Group.

Business model: It generates revenue through cloud software licenses and software development kit subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: The company was founded in 2020, employs around 35 people, and has raised $18 million in Series A and A2 funding rounds.
Geography: The company is based in Iceland and operates globally.

points.description: Standards task group developing measurement procedures for testing loudspeaker sound levels.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops industry-wide standards for measuring and comparing audio equipment, rather than manufacturing commercial products, chips, or software, for specifiers and users in the audio industry.
1. A standards body that develops measurement procedures and test signals distributed as downloadable documents and files.
2. Mathematical test signals that emulate the dynamic characteristics, spectrum, and frequency-dependent crest factor of typical music for use with standard audio analyzers and microphones.
3. Measurement of the maximum linear sound levels of loudspeakers to provide independently verifiable performance benchmarking.
4. Open standards and accompanying test signals made available for download via a website.
5. Measurement and benchmarking of loudspeakers across automotive, consumer electronics, professional audio, post-production, and cinema applications.
6. Specifiers and users of audio equipment across the broader audio industry.
7. Its open standards are used by industry professionals to verify and compare the performance of loudspeakers manufactured by others.
8. It develops test signals mathematically derived from analyzing hundreds of musical selections across all genres to emulate the crest factor of typical music.

2. Artificial intelligence processes and advanced algorithms that differentiate and separate sound sources within mixed audio recordings.

4. Software products and licensed intellectual property containing proprietary source separation algorithms.

8. It was an early entrant into the market and established a position in the niche field of audio source separation.

points.description: Audio technology company offloading complex audio processing from the CPU to the GPU.
points.bullets:

1. A software and developer tools company whose audio plugins and SDK run on consumer GPUs inside desktop digital audio workstations.
2. GPU-accelerated digital signal processing algorithms, including neural network amp modeling and finite impulse response convolution, that execute on graphics processing units.
3. Low-latency multi-channel audio processing, convolution reverb, neural amp modeling and FIR convolution effects.
4. Software plugins for end users and a software development kit for developers.
5. Professional audio production environments, digital audio workstations, studio workflows and live sound processing.
6. Audio professionals, developers, musicians and audio software retailers.
7. Its developer SDK is used by plugin developers to build GPU-accelerated audio effects, and its finished plugins are sold to audio professionals through retailers.
8. It offloads complex audio DSP workloads from the CPU to the GPU to achieve nearly zero latency for pro-level effects.

2. Mathematical frameworks and objective measurement parameters that map digital audio output to human hearing perception and quantify perceived audio degradation.
3. Standardized parameters for room acoustics analysis, objective loudness and sharpness calculation, and perceptual evaluation of audio quality.
4. Published international standards and facilitated intellectual property frameworks.
5. Quality assurance evaluation of digital signal processors, physical transducers, audio compression codecs, consumer tech, professional live sound equipment, and massive venues.
6. Audio engineers, hardware manufacturers, and software developers.

8. It operates as an independent standard-setting authority rather than a market competitor, bridging digital audio theory and physical real-world acoustics.

points.bullets:
A maker of high-end home audio equipment that designs, manufactures and sells turntables, speakers, amplifiers and network music streamers, along with companion control software, for consumers and custom installers.
1. An equipment maker that builds and sells finished audio hardware together with proprietary control applications.
2. The company integrates digital stream management, networked audio rendering, proprietary digital-to-analog conversion and analog electronics within hand-built audio components.
3. The products deliver high-resolution music streaming, multi-room and multi-zone audio distribution, and integration with digital and analog audio sources.
4. The company delivers finished hardware products plus software applications for consumer mobile devices.
5. The equipment is used in home audio systems and custom-installation multi-room residential settings.
6. The company sells to consumers and custom-installation professionals.
7. Its finished hardware is sold direct to end users and through custom integrators, with integrations designed into residential smart-home systems.
8. A "Source First" design philosophy, in-house engineering and proprietary digital-to-analog conversion technology distinguish its hand-built high-end audio products.

Key partners and customers: The company integrates with high-resolution streaming services including TIDAL, Qobuz, Amazon Music and Spotify Connect, and smart-home automation platforms including Crestron and Control4.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: The company makes money through direct sale of premium audio hardware and ongoing software upgrades.
Scale and maturity: The organization is an established manufacturer with long-standing heritage in the audio industry.
Geography: The company is based in Glasgow, United Kingdom, and operates primarily in the home audio market.
Beyond audio: Audio is the company's entire focus.

points.name: Ole Wolff
points.description: Danish manufacturer designing and building audio transducers like speakers, microphones, and headphone drivers.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of acoustic transducers that designs and produces audio components, including MEMS microphones, headphone drivers, speakers, and buzzers, for consumer electronics brands.
1. A component manufacturer that designs and builds acoustic transducers, sold as finished hardware components for integration into devices.
2. Acoustic and magnetic design using MEMS technology for microphones and dynamic moving-coil transducers with stiff piston-area diaphragms for headphone drivers.
3. Sound capture through analog and digital MEMS microphones with high signal-to-noise ratios, and sound reproduction through dynamic headphone drivers, speakers, and magnetic buzzers.
4. Finished hardware components, including analog and PDM digital MEMS microphones, headphone drivers, micro-speakers, and surface-mount buzzers.
5. Earbuds, headphones, development kits for audio devices, and consumer electronics requiring acoustic capture or reproduction.
6. Consumer electronics brands, audio product developers, and development kit providers.
7. Its transducers are designed into earbuds and headphones by consumer electronics brands and integrated into development kits by audio solution providers.
8. Specialized acoustic and magnetic design that produces MEMS microphones with high acoustic overload points and headphone drivers engineered for near-perfect pistonic movement to minimize distortion.

Business model: Hardware sales of acoustic components and transducers.

A maker of professional audio equipment that builds high-end modular analog mixing consoles for recording studios, sold as customized, made-to-order studio centerpiece instruments with interchangeable preamp modules, integrated EQs, patch bays, monitor sections and automation controls.
1. An equipment maker that builds analog mixing consoles and sells them as finished, bespoke hardware installed directly into customers' studios.
2. Modular analog console architecture in which customers choose channel counts and preamp module types, built around vintage-colored and transparent preamp designs, digitally controlled automation for fader, solo and mute functions, and integrated patch bays and monitor sections.
3. Analog mixing, preamp coloration, equalization, signal routing through integrated patch bays, monitor control, and automated fader, solo and mute operation.
4. Finished hardware consoles configured to order, with an online configuration tool that generates quotes and facilitates direct purchase and custom installation.
5. Commercial recording studios, private production studios and high-end engineering rooms.
6. Recording studios, private producers and professional audio engineers buying premium, tailored studio equipment.
7. Its consoles are purchased directly by studios and producers and installed as central pieces of their studio setups.
8. Its console configurator software lets customers visually design a bespoke console with custom channel configurations and real-time pricing, supporting made-to-order analog desks rather than fixed product lines.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A custom 24-input console was installed for Michael McDonald's studio, with a California studio installation completed at Dreamway in partnership with Scott Frankfurt.
Organization type: A privately held equipment manufacturer operating as a direct-to-customer professional audio brand.
Business model: Direct sale and custom installation of professional studio equipment, with quotes and purchases generated through its online console configurator.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus, centered on professional studio mixing equipment and supporting configuration software.

points.name: Alcons Audio
points.description: Dutch professional sound system manufacturer developing pro-ribbon speaker technology for studio and live event audio.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional sound systems that develops and builds loudspeakers, subwoofers, amplified controllers, and stage monitors utilizing proprietary pro-ribbon transducer technology for the studio, cinema, installation, and touring industries.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished loudspeakers, amplifiers, and controllers, sold as complete hardware systems.
2. The core technology is a patented pro-ribbon transducer design combined with Class-D amplification and DSP engines, providing high-output mid and high frequencies with fast-transient response and low distortion.
3. The systems deliver high SPL sound reinforcement, extended low-frequency reproduction, accurate sound monitoring, and spatial audio rendering for immersive environments.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products, including passive and self-powered loudspeakers, subwoofers, and amplified loudspeaker controllers with integrated DSP.
5. The products are used in cinemas, houses of worship, live sound touring, studios, corporate installations, residential home theaters, and immersive experience rooms.
6. The company sells to system designers, consultants, AV integrators, production companies, and premium residential distributors.
7. Its finished hardware systems are designed into venues and touring rigs by integrators and distributed to residential channels by cinema equipment providers.
8. The organization applies the exact same proprietary transducer, amplification, and processing technologies from studio reference monitors to large-scale sound reinforcement, maintaining a single cross-application audio reference.
points.profile:

Organization type: A privately held manufacturer.
Business model: The organization generates revenue through the sale of finished professional audio hardware, loudspeakers, and associated electronic controllers.
Scale and maturity: A European manufacturer founded in 2002 that develops and produces all products in-house.
Geography: Based in the Netherlands with a North American sales operation, operating in global professional audio markets.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio company focused entirely on professional and residential sound reinforcement hardware.

points.name: Algo
points.description: Canadian manufacturer building IP endpoints for paging, emergency alerting, and secure door entry.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures network-based IP audio and visual communication endpoints, including IP speakers, horns, paging adapters, and intercoms, for enterprises transitioning from analog to VoIP unified communication and mass notification systems.
1. An equipment manufacturer that builds IP paging speakers, horns, visual alerters, paging adapters, and intercoms sold as finished hardware endpoints that run on enterprise local area networks.
2. Network-attached audio and visual endpoints that stream voice paging and emergency alerts over IP networks using SIP and multicast protocols, paired with analog-to-IP bridge adapters for legacy speaker integration.
3. Voice paging, public address, background music distribution, loud ringing, emergency mass notification, secure door entry intercoms, and visual alerting.
4. Finished hardware products, including IP endpoints, paging adapters, strobe lights, and endpoint supervision controllers, distributed through reseller and integration partners.
5. Offices, classrooms, hallways, warehouses, yards, manufacturing facilities, healthcare buildings, and educational campuses.
6. Enterprises, educational institutions, healthcare facilities, and manufacturing organizations requiring networked communication and alerting infrastructure.
7. Its finished hardware endpoints are sold, installed, and supported by telecommunications resellers and integration partners for enterprise unified communication and notification deployments.
8. The equipment integrates directly with unified communication platforms and mass notification systems to replace legacy analog paging infrastructure with managed network endpoints.

Organization type: A privately held telecommunications equipment manufacturing company.

points.description: Finnish audio company making throwable wireless audience microphones that auto-mute when tossed.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds throwable and wearable wireless microphone systems for audience engagement in large spaces, selling finished hardware to universities, corporate events, and conference organizers. Its products include a throwable cube microphone, a wearable neck microphone, and a handheld microphone, plus a four-channel wireless system with a DSP-equipped hub receiver.
1. An audio equipment maker that builds wireless microphone systems sold as finished hardware for installation in lecture halls, meeting rooms, and live event venues.
2. Wireless microphone systems operating on the 2.4 GHz band, with motion-sensor-based automuting that silences the microphone when it is thrown, caught, or dropped, and a four-channel hub receiver with built-in digital signal processing and Dante audio-over-IP networking.
3. Audience-engagement audio capture through throwable and wearable wireless microphones, plus automixing, feedback suppression, and auto-equalization on its multi-channel receiver.
4. Finished hardware products, including complete wireless microphone systems and a retrofit module that attaches to existing beltpack transmitters from major microphone brands.
5. Lecture halls and unsupervised classrooms at universities, hybrid meetings, corporate events, conferences, and large venues.
6. Universities, corporate event organizers, and conference organizers, including AV staging companies.
7. Its finished microphone systems are purchased by universities and event organizers and installed as room standards in lecture halls and meeting spaces.
8. Its throwable microphone form factor combined with motion-sensor automuting, which prevents handling noise when the microphone is tossed between audience members, defines a unique niche for engagement-driven audio capture.

points.description: US audio company making invisible surface-mounted speakers for immersive room sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and finished hardware that designs and sells invisible surface-excitation transducers for installed audio, and handcrafted studio monitoring systems for recording professionals.
1. An equipment maker that builds surface-excitation transducers and studio monitor loudspeakers sold as finished physical hardware.
2. The transducers use planar wave physics to excite adhered surfaces into acoustic planar radiating sources, while the monitors use passive crossovers, high-excursion ceramic matrix drivers, and AMT tweeters paired with Class A/B amplification.
3. The transducers deliver invisible room-wide spatial audio with even frequency response and sound pressure levels across large surfaces, and the monitors deliver full-range frequency response and dynamic accuracy for mix translation.
4. The products are sold as finished hardware components and complete stereo monitoring systems.
5. The transducers are used in commercial and residential built-in installations, and the monitors are used in recording, mixing, and mastering studios.
6. The company sells to custom integrators, residential and commercial installers, and recording professionals.
7. Its finished hardware is distributed through authorized dealers and installed directly into architectural surfaces or studio environments.
8. The transducer approach turns standard building materials like drywall and glass into acoustic radiating surfaces to achieve a completely invisible form factor without high-frequency beaming.

points.name: ALC NetworX
points.description: Munich-based R&D center and Lawo subsidiary developing RAVENNA, an open standard for transporting real-time audio over IP networks in broadcast environments.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops and promotes an open-technology standard for real-time audio and media transport over IP networks for professional broadcast and audio manufacturers. It establishes interoperability specifications using standard networking protocols to enable low-latency, reliable signal distribution. The organization operates as a development support arm helping equipment makers achieve broad industry standard compatibility.
1. A standards body that develops networking specifications and protocols which it provides openly to manufacturers to implement in their own audio products.
2. Network protocols operating at Layer 3 of the OSI model utilizing RTP/RTCP, PTPv2, and DNS to route high-resolution, low-latency media data.
3. Low-latency, fully transparent, high-resolution audio signal distribution scaling up to 192 kHz PCM and 384 kHz DSD/DXD at 24-bit depth.
4. Open-technology standards and specifications provided without a proprietary licensing policy for manufacturers to build into their equipment.
5. In-house signal distribution, live event setups, outside broadcast support, inter-studio WAN links, and large-scale commercial AV installations.
6. Professional audio and broadcast manufacturers, as well as networking infrastructure companies.
7. Its specifications are implemented by equipment makers and networking hardware providers into professional broadcast and AV products.
8. It provides a cost-effective, open route for audio manufacturers to achieve AES67 and SMPTE ST 2110 compatibility without proprietary licensing restrictions.

An audio technology company that designs and manufactures high-performance transducers and OEM amplifier modules for audio equipment vendors. The company develops proprietary mathematical models of transducer motor systems and suspensions to optimize signal chain performance and reduce distortion. It sells these components into the home audio sector.
1. A component manufacturer that designs and builds transducers and OEM amplifier modules, sold as finished physical components for integration into audio equipment.
2. Proprietary mathematical models of transducer motor systems, suspensions, domes, and surrounds that optimize performance by independently reducing harmonic and intermodulation distortion mechanisms.
3. The company delivers high-power amplification and low-distortion bass-midwoofer acoustic reproduction.
4. Finished transducer components and OEM amplifier modules.
5. Home audio equipment and stereo amplifiers.
6. Audio equipment vendors.
7. Its OEM amplifier modules and transducers are integrated into finished audio products by consumer electronics brands.
8. Its systematic mathematical modeling of transducer physics independently maps and reduces separate distortion mechanisms without degrading other aspects of the audio signal.
points.profile:

Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Sales of high-performance transducer components and OEM amplifier modules.
Scale and maturity: Established company with notable design wins in the high-end home audio market.
Geography: Operating primarily in the home audio sector.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: EASE
points.description: Acoustic simulation software suite predicting how sound systems perform in 3D room models.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides acoustic simulation software for audio engineers and system designers to build 3D models of spaces and predict how sound systems will perform within them.
1. A developer tools company whose acoustic simulation software runs as a desktop application on Windows computers.
2. Geometric acoustic simulation algorithms that model room geometry, surface materials, and loudspeaker directivity data defined in generic loudspeaker library files.
3. Simulates sound pressure level, speech intelligibility, reverberation times, directivity, and auralisation for loudspeaker configurations in 3D room models.
4. Software products licensed to customers.
5. Concert halls, houses of worship, lecture theaters, and stadiums.
6. Acoustic consultants, technical planners, architects, and sound system integrators.
7. Its simulation software is used by acoustic consultants and system designers to design and verify sound systems for venues.
8. It operates as a brand-agnostic industry standard for acoustic simulation that loudspeaker manufacturers integrate with rather than compete against.
points.profile:

Organization type: A privately held software company.
Business model: Commercial per-seat software licenses.
Scale and maturity: Introduced in 1990, established as an industry standard simulation suite.
Geography: Based in Berlin, Germany.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on acoustic simulation and sound system design software.

points.name: ALCNetworx
points.description: German technology company that invented the RAVENNA protocol for transmitting professional audio over IP networks.
points.bullets:
A technology company that develops the RAVENNA protocol for audio over IP networking, establishing interoperability standards for transmitting uncompressed professional audio over standard IP networks. The organization provides this technology to professional broadcast and audio industries as a foundational networking standard.
1. A technology company that develops an audio over IP networking protocol provided as a licensed specification and standard for equipment manufacturers.
2. The core technology is an audio over IP networking protocol designed to transport uncompressed, low-latency audio over standard Ethernet and IP networks.
3. The protocol delivers audio networking, routing, synchronization, and interoperability capabilities for professional audio signals.
4. Equipment makers and technology providers get the protocol through licensed specifications and interoperability standards.
5. The protocol is used in professional broadcast facilities, audio production environments, and live sound systems.
6. The organization sells to professional audio equipment manufacturers, broadcast technology providers, and system integrators.
7. Its licensed protocol is implemented by equipment manufacturers into their networked audio products.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by focusing on establishing open interoperability standards for IP-based audio rather than selling finished hardware or proprietary software endpoints.

Organization type: The organization is a privately held technology company.
Business model: The company makes money through licensing its networking protocol and specifications to equipment manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: The company operates at an established level within the professional audio and broadcast industry.
Geography: The organization is based and operates internationally within professional audio and broadcast markets.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio networking technology and standards.

points.description: Professional broadcast audio manufacturer building hardware and software for distributing broadcast-grade audio over IP networks.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and software that builds broadcast-grade audio transport and IP distribution systems, selling hardware gateways, network interfaces, and containerized software codecs to broadcasters.
1. An equipment maker and software developer whose audio transport gateways and codecs run as containerized software on commercial off-the-shelf servers and cloud-hosted environments, and as finished hardware appliances.
2. Containerized multi-codec gateways and audio over IP networking interfaces that use standardized encoding algorithms to route multichannel audio across quality-of-service-enabled IP networks.
3. High-density audio transport, studio-to-transmitter links, cloud-to-ground remote distribution, dual diverse-path streaming for redundancy, and scheduled delayed playout.
4. Finished hardware appliances, network interface nodes, and licensed software containers deployed on commercial servers or in cloud environments.
5. Broadcasting studios, transmitter links, and wide-area remote distribution over private WANs, satellite links, and public Internet connections.
6. Broadcasters worldwide who require mission-critical audio contribution and distribution.
7. Its hardware and software are deployed directly by broadcasters into their studio and transmission infrastructure.
8. It transitions legacy hardware-based broadcast transport to flexible, cloud-ready software architectures with per-channel scalable licensing.

points.name: Goer Dynamics B.V.
points.description: Belgian technology company developing immersive audio codecs and licensing 3D sound standards.
points.bullets:
An audio IP licensor and codec developer that licenses immersive audio technologies, wireless audio codecs, and spatial audio creation software, and operates a direct-to-consumer immersive music streaming service. The organization develops the AURO-3D technology stack and the AURO-CX adaptive streaming codec for high-resolution 3D audio delivery, licensing its creative software to professionals while offering finished streaming services to consumers. It leverages a 20-year legacy in spatial audio to bring immersive formats from video into high-resolution music streaming.
1. An audio IP licensor and software developer whose codecs, spatial audio engines, and creative tool suites are licensed to industry partners, and whose streaming platform runs as a consumer application across mobile and home networks.
2. Adaptive bitrate streaming algorithms and spatial audio rendering engines that deliver up to 24-bit/192kHz high-resolution 3D immersive audio while dynamically adjusting to network conditions without downscaling the source file.
3. High-resolution 3D immersive audio delivery, adaptive bitrate streaming, stereo-to-surround upmixing, and spatial audio mixing, creation, and monitoring.
4. Licensed IP and algorithms, software licenses for creative tools, and a direct-to-consumer streaming application.
5. High-resolution music streaming services, professional audio mixing studios, and immersive home or automotive audio systems.
6. Audio professionals, content creators, consumer electronics brands, and direct streaming consumers.
7. Its codec and spatial audio engine are licensed to the broader audio industry for integration into consumer products, and its creative tools are used by professionals to produce content for its consumer streaming platform.
8. The organization extends immersive audio technology from video applications into high-resolution music streaming using adaptive bitrate streaming that preserves studio master quality without requiring specialized playback equipment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization operates as a subsidiary under Goerdyna Holding A/S, positions its format alongside Dolby Atmos, and is supported by the Goerdyna Group's market leadership in premium home loudspeakers and automotive audio.
Organization type: A newly established corporate subsidiary of a holding group.

2. A single-driver sound transducer operating on a unique physical principle that avoids the mechanical mass-spring behavior and transient ringing of conventional multi-way speakers, achieving a fast rise time of 13 microseconds.
3. Reproduction of fine structural sound details, precise localization of voices and instruments, and a realistic three-dimensional soundstage with a maximum permitted frequency deviation of 0.5dB.
4. Finished handmade hardware systems and individual loudspeakers, along with hardware upgrades for older transducers.
5. High-fidelity home audio setups and audiophile listening rooms.
